events.hypothesis: It is unadjudicated for a MEASUREMENT-CONVENTION reason rather than a performance one: a causal attention call does about half the naive 4*B*H*S*S*D work, and no instrument on this campaign has committed to a convention, so the class was skipped rather than scored. Under the causal convention the block runs near its bf16 roofline like the other GEMM classes, because it is a cutlass fmha kernel on regular shapes.

events.supported_if: at or above 0.90 of published on the causal convention, matching s1688 and the grouped expert path

events.because: The frozen criterion reads REFUTED IF the achieved rate on the causal convention comes back BELOW 0.75 of the published 165.2 TF/s. It comes back at 0.388 on the block-causal convention with a 5-matmul backward -- the most generous defensible count, 136 of 256 tiles issued and the recompute charged as work -- and at 0.313 on the least generous. Even the naive square convention returns 0.730, still under the threshold, and that row is self-refuting because it puts the forward at 1.002 of the card's published peak. Every variant the instrument can defend refutes the hypothesis, so this is not a convention artefact. The explanation under test was that the class was unadjudicated for a measurement-convention reason rather than a performance one: the convention hole was real and is now closed, and the conclusion drawn from it was wrong.

events.hypothesis: The refutation does not close the thread, it relocates it. Two things the measurement itself hands over. (1) The backward is 9,479.3 us against a forward of 2,491.1 us, a 3.8x TIME ratio against a 2.0-2.5x FLOP ratio, so the two directions are not equally far from their references and the backward holds most of the 12.0 ms. (2) The trace records the kernel population as fmha_cutlassF/B_bf16_aligned_64x64_..._sm80 -- PyTorch memory-efficient cutlass at Ampere tiles -- which is an observation about WHICH backend ran on an Ada card and not yet a claim that any other backend is available or faster here. The successor asks why the backward specifically sits at 0.35, and it must be measured rather than argued: whether the backend is a choice or the only one this build offers is a source-and-runtime question, not an inference from a rate. Also still open and NOT closed by this refutation: the convention itself, which is now settled and reusable for any later attention measurement on this campaign.

events.observation: The attention backward is 9,479.3 us per step against a forward of 2,491.1 us. That is a 3.8x TIME ratio against a FLOP ratio of 2.0 (four grad matmuls over two forward matmuls) to 2.5 (five, if the score matrix is recomputed). So the backward is roughly 1.5 to 1.9 times further from its reference than the forward, and it holds 9.5 of the block 12.0 ms. The trace also records the kernel population by name: fmha_cutlassF_bf16_aligned_64x64_rf_sm80 and fmha_cutlassB_bf16_aligned_64x64_k64_seqaligned_sm80, which is the PyTorch memory-efficient cutlass path at Sm80 tiles, running on an Ada sm89 card.

events.hypothesis: Mechanism: the SDPA dispatcher never had the flash backend to choose from. The call site is F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q,k,v,is_causal=True) with no mask and bf16 head_dim 64 -- the signature flash is built for -- so a dispatcher holding flash would normally take it. If the flash kernels are absent from this build or unsupported on this platform, every such call falls through to the memory-efficient cutlass path, whose backward is the least tuned kernel of the pair and whose tiles are compiled for Sm80 rather than the card in the socket. That would produce exactly what is observed: a whole attention population on one cutlass symbol, and a backward further from its reference than its own forward.

events.refuted_if: torch on this host reports the FLASH backend as BUILT and SELECTABLE for exactly this call signature -- bf16, head_dim 64, is_causal true, no attn_mask, the strides _document_sdpa actually produces -- because then the dispatcher did hold flash and declined it, and absence cannot be the mechanism. A partial result also refutes: flash built but rejected for a reason OTHER than platform support, such as stride or alignment, refutes the availability explanation and names a different one.
events.supported_if: torch reports the flash backend unavailable for this signature on this build or platform, so the memory-efficient cutlass path was the only one the dispatcher could reach
events.instrument: scripts/issue1945/sdpa_backend_availability.py

events.note: SDPA backend availability probe, three small bf16 tensors + one call, under 2 minutes

events.because: The frozen criterion refutes only if flash is BUILT and SELECTABLE, or built and rejected for a non-platform reason. torch states in its own words: Torch was not compiled with flash attention (sdp_utils.cpp:771, from can_use_flash_attention). is_flash_attention_available() is false and USE_FLASH_ATTENTION does not appear in torch.__config__.show() for 2.10.0+cu126. Both refuting branches require flash to be present and neither obtains, so the dispatcher never had it to choose from and the memory-efficient cutlass path was the only one reachable -- which is what the census sees: one symbol, every call, forward and backward. Tested against tensors built the way _document_sdpa builds them, stride 1048576/64/1024/1 and non-contiguous, because stride eligibility is one of the things flash checks. Note for the successor rather than for this verdict: flash_sdp_enabled() returns TRUE while the kernels are absent, so that flag reports the preference and not the capability.

events.hypothesis: SUPPORTED, and the support hands over a sharper question than the one asked. can_use_cudnn_attention returns TRUE for this exact signature and cudnn_sdp_enabled() is true, yet the dispatcher still took the cutlass memory-efficient path -- one symbol, every call. Priority order, a later runtime check, or the cutlass path genuinely winning selection are all consistent with what was observed and the probe cannot distinguish them. That is measurable and it is cheaper to measure than to argue. What this does NOT license: it does not say a flash-enabled build or the cudnn backend would be faster at this geometry. Nothing was compared and nothing was timed, and asserting a saving would be a claim about what a change collects. It also does not make swapping the torch build a treatment -- the build is part of the declared execution environment every governed receipt binds to, so changing it carries its own equivalence question rather than being a kernel swap.

events.observation: torch reports can_use_cudnn_attention TRUE for the exact signature the decoder issues, and cudnn_sdp_enabled() is also true, yet a one-call profile shows the dispatcher selecting fmha_cutlassF_bf16_aligned_64x64_rf_sm80 -- the memory-efficient cutlass symbol -- and the full census shows that same symbol on every one of the 24 forward and 24 backward calls per step. An eligible backend that is never reached is either lower in the priority order or failing a check that eligibility does not cover.

events.hypothesis: Mechanism: backend PRIORITY, not capability. With flash absent from the build, the dispatcher walks its remaining preference list, and if EFFICIENT_ATTENTION sits ahead of CUDNN_ATTENTION for this device then cudnn is never consulted no matter what its eligibility check would have said. can_use_cudnn_attention answers a question the dispatcher never asks in this configuration, which is why the two disagree.

events.refuted_if: with sdpa_kernel(SDPBackend.CUDNN_ATTENTION) forced for the identical call, the dispatch still lands on a cutlass memory-efficient symbol, or raises -- because then cudnn is not actually reachable for this signature, the eligibility report was not actionable, and ORDERING is not the mechanism

events.because: Frozen criterion: REFUTED IF with sdpa_kernel(SDPBackend.CUDNN_ATTENTION) forced for the identical call, the dispatch still lands on a cutlass memory-efficient symbol, or raises. Neither obtained: forced CUDNN dispatched cudnn_generated_fort_native_sdpa_sm80_flash_fprop_wmma_f16_knob_6_128x64x64_4x1x1_kernel0_0 plus a device memset, distinct from the unforced cutlass symbol, with no raise and no cutlass fallback. Forced FLASH raised RuntimeError No available kernel. So cudnn IS reachable for this signature and the dispatcher does not go there. The MECHANISM I named is refuted by the same run: sdp_utils.cpp:680 cuDNN attention has been runtime disabled fired during the UNFORCED call, so it was considered and refused by a runtime disable, not skipped by priority ordering.

events.hypothesis: WHAT THE REFUTATION DID NOT CLOSE. The runtime disable is not explained: this says nothing about WHY cudnn attention is disabled in this build (platform guard, version guard, or a defaults choice), nor whether it can be enabled at all outside a forced context manager. Nothing was timed, so cudnn-vs-cutlass speed at this geometry is entirely open. WHAT ARITHMETIC NOW CLOSES, and it closes the whole attention thread as an ARM. The attention block is 11,970.5 us of a 175,190 us governed step = 6.83 percent. Driving attention to ZERO gives 1.073x. The standing bar (1945-multiplicative-movement-only clause 1) refuses any arm whose pre-stated ceiling is below 1.5x, so NO attention treatment -- cudnn dispatch, flash rebuild, tiling -- can be dispatched as an arm on this campaign. That is a route ruling from measurement, not an exit ruling on the target. The attention adjudication was still worth its cost: it removed a 12 ms block from the candidate set by measurement rather than by assumption. SUCCESSOR, chosen by SHARE of the remaining factor rather than by authoring cost. The elementwise class is 27,862.9 us -- 15.9 percent of the step, the largest non-GEMM block measured, and the biggest single lever on the table. The census scored it at 1.151 of published DRAM bandwidth. A rate ABOVE the card's published DRAM rate is impossible for genuinely DRAM-resident traffic, exactly as the square-convention attention row was impossible at 1.002 of peak. So one of two things is true and they have opposite consequences: either the bytes are largely cache-resident, in which case DRAM is the wrong roofline and the block has real unmeasured distance against an L2 roofline; or the byte figure derived from recorded input dims is wrong, in which case every bandwidth number in the census inherits the error. Either answer is load-bearing and the discriminator reads a trace already on disk.

events.observation: The non-GEMM bandwidth census records 5.18 ms per step of pure aten::copy_ inside the elementwise class -- kernels that move bytes and compute nothing. Its own not_closed line (a) says the BYTE-REDUCTION direction is untouched and unsized, and that this is where the ~40.6 ms of bandwidth-bound work lives. Separately, ember_v0_decoder.py at the governed-hour head expands the key and value tensors 4x before every attention call, at three sites: line 627/628 in _attention, lines 756/757 in the ragged branch, and lines 765/766. k.repeat_interleave(4, dim=1) on a GQA layout materialises four identical copies of every KV head purely so the tensor shape matches the 16 query heads.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM: repeat_interleave cannot be a view. It allocates a new tensor and writes every element, so each attention call pays a full materialisation of k and v at four times their stored size, per layer, per step, in both the forward and (as a saved-tensor re-expansion or a gradient reduction) the backward. That is data movement with no arithmetic attached -- exactly the signature of the aten::copy_ mass the census measured but did not attribute. If the mechanism holds, the copies are STRUCTURALLY AVOIDABLE rather than incidental: the attention backends accept broadcast KV directly, so the expansion exists to satisfy a shape check rather than to feed a computation. WHY THIS IS WORTH ASKING RATHER THAN ASSUMING: the census attributed bytes to CLASSES and never to CALL SITES, so 5.18 ms of copy is currently an unowned quantity. An unowned millisecond invites exactly the error this campaign keeps making -- naming a plausible source and treating the naming as the measurement. The trace already carries the kernel->correlation->innermost cpu_op join that answers it.

events.refuted_if: Joining every aten::copy_ (and every copy-family kernel counted in the class census's copy population) to its innermost cpu_op in the captured trace shows that call sites attributable to the GQA key/value expansion -- aten::repeat_interleave, aten::expand followed by a materialising copy, or a copy whose recorded input dims carry the 4-head KV shape and whose output carries the 16-head shape -- account for LESS THAN HALF the copy device time. Below half, the GQA expansion is not the copy mass, the 5.18 ms is owned by something else, and the mechanism named here is wrong regardless of how avoidable repeat_interleave is in principle.
events.supported_if: GQA-attributable call sites account for at least half the copy device time, which would make the expansion the largest single owner of pure data movement in the step and give the byte-reduction direction its first named, source-bound site.
events.instrument: scripts/issue1945/copy_mass_attribution.py

events.note: analysis-only: reads cia-captured-trace-20260914T183257Z.json already on disk, no card, no lease
fraction 0.0505 against a 0.5 refutation line

events.because: Frozen criterion: REFUTED IF GQA-attributable call sites account for LESS THAN HALF the copy device time. Measured 376.9 us of 7,462.7 us = 0.0505, an order of magnitude below the line, so the verdict does not turn on where the threshold sat. The GQA expansion is real and present exactly where the source said (aten::copy_ on [4096,4,4,64], 48 calls/step, 357.4 us) -- it is 5 percent of the copies, not half. The error was the leap from a correct source reading to a MAGNITUDE claim, which source cannot answer.

events.hypothesis: NOT CLOSED BY THIS REFUTATION: (a) it does not say the copies are unavoidable, only that they are small -- a fusion keeping the 32768-wide intermediate in place is still correct work, just not a 1945 arm; (b) it does not size the DOCUMENT-BATCHING BOUNDARY as a whole -- copies are one cost of it, and its launch structure, dependency edges and effect on concurrency are untouched; (c) it does not refute the byte-reduction direction the class census left open, it refutes one named owner and identifies two better ones (the wide-intermediate reassembly at 3,000 us in FOUR calls, and the 3072-wide projection copies at 3,291 us in 86 calls). WHAT THE LAST THREE CYCLES HAVE ESTABLISHED, and it is a pattern rather than three results. Attention is 6.83 percent of the step; the whole pure-copy population is 5.72 percent of summed device time; the sub-5us launch population was already refuted as below the bar; row 1 was refuted as an idle-removal arm. Every INDIVIDUAL class examined is too small to clear 1.5x on its own. That is not an impossibility statement about the target -- it is a route finding, and it points at the one remaining measured structure that is not a single class. SUCCESSOR. The non-GEMM census split the step into a 71.4 ms compute-bound population and a ~40.6 ms bandwidth-bound population. The overlap row (overlap-bandwidth-bound-with-compute-bound-work) is on the registry as INCONCLUSIVE precisely because it lacked that split, and it now has it. events.observation: The optimizer block spends 16,817.8 us per step moving at most 6.64 GB, which is 39.15 percent of what the card publishes -- so roughly 60 percent of the streaming capacity is idle during a kernel that does nothing but stream. The shape of the work is unusual and the numbers are all measured: 21.3 multi_tensor_apply launches per step, 351 tensors of very unequal size (from 1,024 elements at final_norm to 33,554,432 at the embedding), packed by multi_tensor_apply into batches capped at 36 tensors or 320 chunks of 64 Ki elements. That packing means the final batch of every launch is partial, and it means a 1,024-element tensor consumes a whole tensor slot in the metadata while contributing one chunk. 15,847.4 of the 16,817.8 us is the fused AdamW symbol itself; the remaining 970 us is _foreach_zero_ and _foreach_add_.

events.hypothesis:
THE MECHANISM, and the three candidates it separates. multi_tensor_apply assigns one thread block per 64 Ki-element chunk and launches when either the 36-tensor metadata cap or the 320-block cap is hit. Whichever cap binds decides the shape of the inefficiency, and they predict different things.
(1) TENSOR-CAP BOUND. If launches are ending on the 36-tensor cap rather than the 320-chunk cap, the kernel is issuing far fewer than 320 blocks per launch and the card is underfilled by construction -- a grid too small to saturate, repeated 21 times. The stepped set is 351 tensors and 7,233 chunks, so an even packing would give 23 launches at ~315 blocks each and the tensor cap would bind on 9.75 launches; the two caps are close enough here that which one binds is a per-launch question, not a global one, and it can be read from the trace by joining each launch to its grid dimensions.
(2) CHUNK-TAIL BOUND. Every launch has a partial final chunk per tensor, and a 1,024-element tensor still costs a full block. With tensor sizes spanning four orders of magnitude the wasted fraction of each block could be large, and it would show as a grid that is nominally full while most threads exit immediately.
(3) OCCUPANCY BOUND. FusedAdamMathFunctor holds four tensor-list pointers plus the running moments in registers; if register pressure caps resident warps the SMs cannot cover DRAM latency regardless of grid size, and no amount of repacking helps.
These prescribe different treatments -- (1) and (2) are fixed by repacking or by a single flattened update over a contiguous state buffer, which is a layout change with no byte saving; (3) is fixed by a different kernel or not at all. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE PER-LAUNCH GRID GEOMETRY, which the trace already carries: each kernel event records its grid and block dimensions. Joining the 21.3 launches to their grids says immediately whether the launches are ending on the tensor cap (small grids) or the chunk cap (grids at or near 320 blocks).

events.refuted_if: The per-launch grid geometry of the 21.3 multi_tensor_apply launches, read from the trace kernel events, shows a MEDIAN grid of AT LEAST 288 blocks -- 90 percent of the 320-block cap. That refutes the tensor-cap reading: the launches would then be ending on the chunk cap with nearly full grids, the card would not be underfilled by the packing, and repacking the tensor list could not be the lever. SUPPORTED IF the median grid is BELOW 288 blocks: the launches are ending on the 36-tensor metadata cap before they fill their block budget, the grid is smaller than the kernel could issue, and a repack or a flattened contiguous update is a real lever on a block this measurement has already shown is not byte-limited. THE 288 FIGURE IS 90 PERCENT OF A SOURCE CONSTANT (depth_to_max_blocks[3] = 320 in MultiTensorApply.cuh), not a hardware limit and not a performance target. Either branch leaves occupancy untested, because this trace carries no occupancy counter; the criterion discriminates candidates (1) and (2) from each other and neither confirms nor refutes (3), and the ruling must say so.

THE CAP ATTRIBUTION IS UNANIMOUS AND IT IS THE FINDING. Grid distribution over 128 launches: 320 blocks x122, 222 x4, 46 x2. Holding out the six terminal launches -- one per step, which end on list exhaustion rather than on any cap -- 122 OF 122 INTERIOR LAUNCHES ENDED ON THE 320-BLOCK CHUNK CAP AND NOT ONE ENDED ON THE 36-TENSOR METADATA CAP. Candidate (1), the tensor-cap reading, is dead.

THE INVENTORY SAYS THE SAME THING INDEPENDENTLY. Simulating the greedy multi_tensor_apply walk over the cycle-9 stepped set and recording WHICH cap terminated each launch gives 22 chunk-cap terminations plus one exhaustion and ZERO tensor-cap terminations; core+expert0 gives 17 and one, also zero. The reason is the size distribution: 351 tensors over 7,342 chunks is 20.9 chunks per tensor, so 36 tensors is about 750 chunks and the block cap is reached first almost every time, and the largest single tensor is 33,554,432 elements = 512 chunks, which alone exceeds the 320-block cap. The tensor cap could still have bound had the 110 one-chunk tensors been contiguous in list order; they are not.

CANDIDATE (2), THE CHUNK TAIL, IS REFUTED AS A SIDE EFFECT BY ARITHMETIC THAT NEEDED NO NEW MEASUREMENT. Dispatched thread slots for the 351-tensor population are 7,342 chunks x 65,536 = 481,165,312 against 474,030,080 elements, so 7,135,232 slots do no work: 1.48 percent. For core+expert0 it is 1.94 percent. A mechanism worth under 2 percent cannot account for a block running at roughly a third of the card streaming rate. Those numbers were in cycle 9 inventory the whole time.

A THIRD AND FINER ESTIMATE OF THE STEPPED POPULATION, WHICH TIGHTENS CYCLE 9 AND MOVES IT IN THE FLATTERING DIRECTION, SO IT IS STATED AS RECHECKABLE ARITHMETIC. events.hypothesis:
MECHANISM. Published DRAM bandwidth is a peak figure under ideal access. Real kernels lose to access granularity, read/write turnaround on the memory bus, ECC-free but imperfect row-buffer locality, and -- under CUPTI instrumentation -- whatever serialization the profiler imposes. A host that demonstrates 472 GB/s on its best-observed read+write stream has an EMPIRICAL envelope, and every achieved-rate claim on this campaign should be read against that envelope rather than against the spec.

WHAT MAKES THIS TESTABLE RATHER THAN RHETORICAL. The trace contains 138 distinct kernel symbols inside the measured-step windows. A subset of them have element counts derivable purely from launch geometry and byte models derivable purely from their functor signature -- the vectorized_elementwise family encodes vec_size and operand count in the symbol itself. Computing achieved bandwidth across every qualifying shape whose traffic exceeds twice the 72 MB L2 gives an empirical envelope built from this trace, on this host, under this instrumentation, with no spec figure anywhere in it.

WHY THIS OUTRANKS RE-ATTACKING OCCUPANCY. The operator directive is that the next event worth reporting is a source-bound measurement showing a LARGE MULTIPLICATIVE movement. Occupancy, if confirmed, is worth at most the 1.49x the occupancy ratio allows on a 16.8 ms block -- about 5 ms of a 175 ms step, under 3 percent. The denominator question is worth more than any of that, because it decides whether the optimizer block is a 2.6x opportunity or a 1.22x one, and therefore whether ANY optimizer treatment belongs on the critical path at all. An answer of "the block is near the machine demonstrated envelope" redirects the campaign to the levers that change how many optimizer steps happen rather than how fast one is -- which is the contract lever, the operator decision that ten cycles have now backed.

Then the 471.7 GB/s point was shape-specific, this host does stream read+write well above it, and fused AdamW at 386.2 GB/s really is far below the machine demonstrated capability -- the framing of cycles 9 through 11 stands and the denominator hypothesis is refuted.

SUPPORTED IF the maximum is AT OR BELOW 700 GB/s: the empirical read+write envelope of this host under this instrumentation sits between roughly 472 and 700, fused AdamW at 386.2 is within 1.82x of the best rate anything in this trace achieves, and the "third of streaming rate" framing overstated the opportunity by using a spec denominator.

hypotheses.explanation:
MECHANISM -- four independent defects in one ten-row table, each one line of source:
  (1) NO PATTERN EXISTS for the optimizer, for sort, or for loss. 16,817.8 us/step was never mislabelled, it was UNLABELLED, and `other` silently served as "I have no name for this".
  (2) THE GROUPED-EXPERT CONTRACTION IS NAMED `_rows` AND `_weights` -- bare Triton kernel names with no prefix. The triton_fused pattern is ^triton_, so it cannot match them, and 18,068.1 us/step of the largest compute class in the step falls through.
  (3) CASE SENSITIVITY APPLIED INCONSISTENTLY: index_scatter_gather and reduce carry no re.I while gemm_bf16, gemm_other, attention and softmax all do, so vectorized_gather_kernel (lowercase) and the five EmbeddingBackwardKernel symbols (capital E) all miss.
  (4) A PATTERN THAT CANNOT EVER FIRE: reduce matches the literal "cub::" and the mangled spelling here is at_cuda_detail3cub with no colons. A regex no input can satisfy is the persistent-lock-file shape living inside a classifier.
A FIFTH, found while reading the table for this cycle and not named by cycle 8: gemm_other matches gemm|sgemm|cutlass|dot_kernel but NOT gemv, so three cuBLAS gemvx symbols (52.1 us) fell through on a spelling one letter away from a pattern that was already there.

WHY IT PROPAGATES. Five scripts IMPORT classify or CLASSES from this module: captured_class_bandwidth, captured_kernel_inventory_and_idle, population_overlap, serialization_is_forced, and other_class_symbol_census. population_overlap additionally derives its compute-bound / bandwidth-bound split from CLASSES MEMBERSHIP, which is where cycle 6 got 52,707.2 and 41,901.3.

AND A SIXTH CONSUMER IS COUPLED BY COPY, NOT BY IMPORT. captured_elementwise_bandwidth.py restates the elementwise regex inline, commented "matched to captured_device_time_classes.py so the population is the SAME class". Correcting the table will not reach it. Cycle 8 named three consumers; there are six, and one of them cannot be fixed by this repair. That is named now so the repair does not appear to cover it.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THE OBSERVATION FALSE. If each downstream consumer selected its own population by its own predicate and used classify only to LABEL output rows, the corrected table would change what rows are called and not what any of them measures. That is plainly possible for captured_kernel_inventory_and_idle, whose use is `classified_as: classify(k)` on a top-kernel listing -- annotation, not selection.

events.observation: THE ROUTE ARITHMETIC AT THIS HEAD LEAVES EXACTLY ONE STACK ABOVE THE 1.5x ARM BAR, and every number in it is already measured and on disk -- this cycle exists because a discriminator in hand must be APPLIED rather than re-derived, and the lane owes a TREATMENT rather than another measurement. Governed step 0.16376 s; terminal 0.0512 s = 3.20x. Device union 131,055.6 us, strictly one kernel at a time on stream 7. GEMM+attention 52,490 us = 40.0% of the union, and the terminal budget is 51.2 ms, so the terminal is ENTIRELY SPENT inside that one class. Inside it the linear population is NOT slow: s1688 32,006 us at 158.9 TF/s = 96.2% of the published dense bf16 rate, s16816 8,518 us at 117.0, cross-checked against the counterpart dimension-derived 6.08 TF/step. So no bf16 kernel-quality, scheduling or fusion treatment acts on those milliseconds: only PRECISION or fewer FLOPs per position does. On the FP8 side the contractions ALREADY beat bf16 -- forward 0.796, dX 0.629 -- and the end-to-end loss is the WRAPPER, whose dominant site is amax at 346.590 us = 59.1% of it. On the non-GEMM side both factor-table rows are refuted AS STANDALONE ARMS at this head: row 1 (kernel-count regime) and row 3 (overlap behind compute) bound idle removal at 32,700 us = 1.25x, and the whole elementwise class is 27,500 us = 1.20x. Each alone is under the bar; nothing has ever measured them as ONE arm, which is what clause 2 of 1945-multiplicative-movement-only requires.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM, STATED BEFORE ANY ARITHMETIC AND SEPARATED FROM IT. The stack is two treatments acting on DISJOINT milliseconds: (i) FP8 at the aten::mm sites, which changes the arithmetic rate at which the 6.08 TF of linear work is performed and touches no non-GEMM kernel; (ii) the combined non-GEMM treatment -- device-idle removal plus elementwise consolidation -- which changes how much non-GEMM device time and host-dispatch gap the step contains and touches no GEMM kernel. They do not contend, which is the condition clause 4 of treatment-selection-states-its-ceiling requires before two ceilings may be composed at all. THE LOAD-BEARING PREMISE, WHICH IS THE THING THAT CAN BE WRONG AND IS NOT ARITHMETIC: that FP8 collects the contraction win end to end rather than spending it on the wrapper. The measured FP8 row says the contractions win and the wrapper loses, so the arm is only real if the wrapper cost is addressed -- amax is 59.1% of it, and delayed scaling over an amax history rather than a per-call current-scaling amax is the named candidate. NO TREATMENT EXISTS FOR IT YET and none is claimed here. [CANDIDATE CLAIM] the arithmetic, on the premise that each treatment collects its own class and nothing else: FP8 at twice the tensor rate puts 6.08 TF at about 18.4 ms; attention stays 12.0 ms; so GEMM+attention 52.5 -> 30.4 ms. The combined non-GEMM lever removes 60.2 ms (32.7 idle + 27.5 elementwise). Step 163.76 - 52.5 + 30.4 - 60.2 = 81.5 ms = 2.01x. FP8 ALONE is 141.7 ms = 1.16x and is REFUSED by clause 1 of 1945-multiplicative-movement-only; the non-GEMM stack alone is 1.58x. Only the two together clear the bar with room, and 2.01x is still short of the 3.20x the terminal needs -- which is a statement about which routes act on which milliseconds, not an impossibility claim and not an exit. The remaining distance is positions per optimizer step, which is a CONTRACT change and the operator decision, and whose own honest projection at this head is about 1.1x rather than the multiple the pre-capture arithmetic implied.

events.refuted_if: The STACKED arm, measured at the governed 1,024-warmed-update geometry on the idle card, delivers a governed p10 BELOW 35,070.3 applied positions/s -- that is, below 1.50x the standing 23,380.183126331838, which is the bar clause 1 of 1945-multiplicative-movement-only sets for dispatching an arm at all. The baseline is the standing governed number and is NOT re-measured for this comparison; if it moves before the arm runs, the bar moves with it and the receipt says so.
events.supported_if: The same arm delivers a governed p10 of 35,070.3 applied positions/s OR MORE. --- INCONCLUSIVE IS THE CORRECT VERDICT, NOT A FALLBACK, IF THE ARM UNDER TEST IS NOT THE STACK. Four branches, each about a way the run could be a different experiment than the one predicted: (a) FP8 IS NOT ACTUALLY ACTIVE at the aten::mm sites carrying the 6.08 TF, verified by the DISPATCHED KERNEL SYMBOLS in the arm own trace and never by a configuration flag -- a source- level precision guarantee is not the compiled one, which this campaign has already been caught by once. (b) THE NON-GEMM TREATMENT IS NOT PRESENT: the measured elementwise class device union plus measured device idle has not fallen by at least HALF of the 60.2 ms the stack assumes (32.7 ms idle + 27.5 ms elementwise at this head). Half, not all, because the criterion tests whether the STACK was run, not whether it was run perfectly -- a partial non-GEMM treatment is still the stack and its shortfall belongs in the verdict, while an absent one is a different arm. (c) THE EQUIVALENCE INSTRUMENT REFUSES THE ARM NUMERICS. An arm that changes the learning contract is not this arm, and gate C licences the number or there is no number. (d) THE RUN IS PROFILED. A profiled number is not a governed number -- the separation clause of the governed-run evidence contract -- and the trace this campaign has been reading has a window span near 590,000 us against a governed step of 175,190, so instrumentation dominates it. --- DISCLOSED BEFORE THE RUN, so the sketch cannot be quietly revised afterwards: I expect the stack to land BETWEEN 1.5x and 2.0x, BELOW the 2.01x the arithmetic gives, because two costs in it are unpriced -- the FP8 wrapper (whose dominant site, amax, is 346.590 us = 59.1% of it, and for which NO TREATMENT EXISTS YET) and whatever kernels the non-GEMM consolidation itself adds. Both push the same way, so a result ABOVE 2.01x would be the surprising one and would mean I have mis-sized a class rather than mis-sized a treatment.
events.instrument: The governed 1,024-update measurement at the merged head of the stacked arm, on the idle card, UNPROFILED, with its evidence package per the governed-run evidence contract. Baseline is the standing governed p10, not a re-run control. THE ARM DOES NOT EXIST YET: this criterion is frozen before authoring precisely so the bar cannot be chosen to fit the result. The authoring order is forced by the load-bearing premise stated at EXPLAINED -- the FP8 wrapper cost must be addressed before FP8 can collect its contraction win end to end, so the first sub-leg is a treatment for the amax site (delayed scaling over an amax history rather than per-call current scaling), and that sub-leg is itself unauthored and unsized.

events.observation: THE HALF OF THE SELECTED ROUTE THAT SURVIVED THIS HOUR IS BUILT ON A 60.2 ms FIGURE WHOSE MECHANISMS ARE ALREADY INDIVIDUALLY REFUTED IN MY OWN REGISTRY, AND I QUOTED IT ANYWAY. Cycle 17 refuted the 2x premise under the FP8 half, which leaves the non-GEMM half as the whole route: 32.7 ms of device idle plus 27.5 ms of elementwise, composed as one 60.2 ms lever worth 1.58x. Querying the registry in that composition own vocabulary -- idle, graph, capture, eager, elementwise, consolidation, launch, adjacency -- returns three rows that bound its parts, and the first query I ran (device idle removable collectible gap between kernels) returned NOTHING, so the widen clause of a-not-closed-line-is-a-claim-about-the-past is what surfaced them. (1) gap-removal-scheduling-bound [REFUTED]: perfect removal of every outside-union interval with the kernel union held fixed is 190,031.6 / 150,052.5 = 1.266x, below the bar. That is the idle term. (2) nongemm-launch-consolidation-bound-is-3.9ms-not-55ms-20260914 [REFUTED]: the whole non-GEMM launch-overhead REMOVAL bound is 3.88 ms, not the ~55 ms the factor-dominant table row 1 assigned it. (3) elementwise-class-is-bandwidth-bound-not-launch-bound-20260914 [REFUTED]: the elementwise launch ceiling alone is 2.65 ms, because the class is bandwidth-bound rather than launch-bound. So "consolidate the elementwise class" collects single-digit milliseconds, not 27.5, and "remove the idle" is separately bounded at 1.266x -- and gap-removal own not_closed line warns in as many words that the gap and eager terms are VERY LIKELY THE SAME MECHANISM COUNTED TWICE. The 60.2 ms composition adds them as if they were independent, which is precisely what clause 4 of treatment-selection-states-its-ceiling forbids. WHAT THE SAME THREE ROWS LEAVE OPEN, IN THEIR OWN WORDS, IS ONE MECHANISM: BYTE REDUCTION. "The BYTE-REDUCTION direction is entirely open and is where the 25.2 ms lives: fusion that keeps intermediates in registers, and elimination of the 5.18 ms of pure aten::copy_. Nothing here refutes it and nothing here sizes it." The sibling row puts the same opening at ~40.6 ms across the whole non-GEMM path. Beside it, two narrower openings: consolidation as an ENABLER of concurrency by reducing dependency edges (named not_closed in both rows, never measured), and L2 residency, unmeasured, with three classes reporting above the published DRAM rate on a ~25 MB working set in a 72 MB L2. THE QUESTION THIS CYCLE MUST ANSWER IS THEREFORE NOT "IS THE NON-GEMM HALF WORTH 1.58x" -- it is "how much of the 25.2 ms of elementwise time is actually BYTES THAT A FUSION WOULD NOT MOVE", which is the only term in the composition that no row has bounded. Nothing is claimed here: this is the observation, and the mechanism and the criterion are the next two stages.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM, STATED BEFORE ANY ARITHMETIC. Device idle and device kernel time are disjoint intervals, so adding 32.7 ms of idle to 27.5 ms of elementwise is not double-counting in the TIMELINE sense, and that is exactly why the composition looked safe. The double count, if it exists, is in the MECHANISMS. A treatment that consolidates or fuses elementwise kernels does not only delete their device time: it deletes the per-launch dispatch holes those kernels created. So a hole sitting between two elementwise kernels is a hole the elementwise treatment plausibly collects BY ITSELF, and crediting it a second time to a separate "remove the idle" treatment counts one act twice. A hole sitting between two GEMM kernels is out of that treatment reach and is genuinely the idle term own. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THEREFORE THE CLASS ON EACH SIDE OF EACH HOLE, and it is computable from a capture already on disk: walk the device-time union per measured step window, and for every interior hole record the class of the kernel that ends on its left and the class of the kernel that starts on its right, using the same class table the millisecond figures come from. WHY THIS DECIDES SOMETHING. Perfect collection of the whole 60.2 ms is 1.58x, which clears the 1.5x arm bar by 0.08. Every part of that composition is separately refuted already -- idle removal alone at 1.266x, non-GEMM launch removal at 3.88 ms, the elementwise launch ceiling at 2.65 ms -- so the composition is the ONLY thing holding the route above the bar, and it holds only if the two terms are independent. If they are not, no non-GEMM composition with a defensible ceiling above the bar currently exists, and the honest consequence is that the route set is empty pending a measured byte-reduction bound rather than that some smaller arm is next. THE ASYMMETRY IS DELIBERATE AND IS NOT A LOOPHOLE: adjacency is NECESSARY for the same-mechanism reading and not SUFFICIENT, because a hole between two elementwise kernels may be a dependency stall or a memory-system wait that survives any consolidation. So a large treatable-adjacent share WITHDRAWS SUPPORT from the independence premise rather than proving the terms identical, and a small share would positively support it. The composition needs the premise supported; it is not enough for it to be merely unrefuted.

events.refuted_if: MORE THAN 50% of interior device idle, measured per step window across the capture, touches a kernel of the non-GEMM TREATABLE set on at least one side. Treatable set, fixed here and not after the numbers: elementwise, triton_fused, cat_copy, index_scatter_gather, softmax, reduce, memcpy, optimizer, loss, sort. It is deliberately WIDE because the route own framing is "the whole non-GEMM side", and a wide set makes the share LARGER -- so the choice works against the composition I am testing, and a narrower reading would make my own refutation weaker rather than stronger. The 50% line is the point at which the reachable holes stop being a minority effect and the remainder can no longer carry the independence premise. WHAT IS REFUTED IS THE INDEPENDENCE PREMISE of the 60.2 ms composition, not the idle term, not the elementwise term, and not any treatment.

MY SKETCH, recorded so it can be wrong: I expect REFUTED with a treatable-adjacent share well above 50%, because the elementwise population is the numerous one (thousands of small kernels against hundreds of GEMMs) so most holes should have an elementwise neighbour by sheer count. A treatment that consolidates or fuses elementwise kernels does not only delete their device time: it deletes the per-launch dispatch holes those kernels created. GENEROSITY IS THE POINT AND IT RUNS AGAINST MY OWN VERDICT. WHAT IS ALREADY WRITTEN, SO THIS CYCLE DOES NOT CLAIM IT AS NEW. rows-1-and-3-candidate-20260914.md section 6 already states, as a [CANDIDATE CLAIM] in prose, that the bf16 GEMM class alone is 52.5 ms against a 51.2 ms terminal and that therefore no treatment acting outside the GEMM class can reach the terminal however perfectly effective. The headline direction of this cycle is NOT a discovery. What does not exist anywhere is the COMPLETE composition: every measured class given its most generous lawful disposition at once, with the non-device time removed too, run through an instrument that refuses an unmentioned class -- and therefore a NUMBER for the best case rather than a statement that one lever is insufficient. THE INPUTS ARE ON DISK AND CONSISTENT. Cycle 18 established that the v2 class unions sum exactly to the device union for this trace (130,996.2 us/step, all thirteen classes) and that this profiled union agrees with the governed union 131,055.6 to 0.05 percent, so the UNION is the one quantity that transfers across the profiled/governed boundary while the span does not. Cycle 13 established zero kernel concurrency on this trace, which is what makes the class unions additive at all.
hypotheses.explanation: MECHANISM. Partition the governed step into ARITHMETIC device time, NON-ARITHMETIC device time and NON-DEVICE time, then give every non-arithmetic term the most generous lawful disposition a treatment could earn and see what step remains. Arithmetic classes RETAIN, because no scheduling or fusion treatment deletes the multiply-accumulates a 3B model owes per token -- only a precision change, a cheaper algorithm, or fewer positions does, and all three are OUTSIDE the non-arithmetic route set this cycle bounds. GENEROSITY IS THE POINT AND IT RUNS AGAINST MY OWN VERDICT. Every non-arithmetic class is credited with its ENTIRE device time going to zero, which no measured treatment on this campaign has come close to: the elementwise launch ceiling measured 2.65 ms against a 27.4 ms class, and whole non-GEMM launch removal measured 3.88 ms against a 60.2 ms non-GEMM path. The non-device time -- all 32.8 ms of host dispatch idle -- is removed in full as well. So the composed step is an UPPER BOUND on the win from every non-arithmetic mechanism stacked perfectly, and a refutation at that bound is stronger than one at any realistic figure. THE OPTIMIZER IS THE ONE CLASS I CANNOT HONESTLY REMOVE. Its 16.8 ms is real arithmetic that no fusion into a GEMM epilogue absorbs, so it is declared work:true and given the most generous lawful disposition instead: a MUTUAL OVERLAP with gemm_bf16, which is the factor-table row-3 proposal (per-layer optimizer on a second stream as backward finishes each layer) at perfect effectiveness. The instrument composes a mutual overlap as max rather than sum, so the optimizer costs zero additional milliseconds. WHY THE INSTRUMENT RATHER THAN THE ARITHMETIC. scripts/issue1945/composition_bound.py exists and refuses exactly the moves that make this kind of bound wrong: an unmentioned class (CLASS_UNMENTIONED), a REMOVES on real arithmetic (WORK_CANNOT_BE_REMOVED), a one-sided overlap that credits the same milliseconds twice (OVERLAP_NOT_MUTUAL), a replacement cost inferred from the incumbent (REPLACEMENT_COST_NOT_MEASURED), and a quantity with no source (MEASUREMENT_UNPROVENANCED). Doing this by hand is one division; doing it through the tool is the same division with five ways to be caught.

The hypothesis under test is that the non-arithmetic route set can reach 80,000 applied positions/s at this geometry; REFUTED means it cannot, at any effectiveness, and therefore that every remaining route lies in arithmetic time (precision at the GEMM sites, a cheaper algorithm, fewer FLOPs) or in positions per optimizer step, which is a CONTRACT change and the operator s decision. THIS BOUNDS THE ROUTE AND NOT THE EXIT. It is not an impossibility claim about the target, it is not rulable as one, and no artifact of this cycle may pre-build that case: measurement selects the route, never the exit, and impossibility is the operator s to rule from receipts.

hypotheses.not_closed: WHAT THIS REFUTATION DOES NOT CLOSE: (1) IT IS ONE GEOMETRY. 4,096 positions per update, CIA-3B, one checkpoint, one capture, no matched-run variation. The arithmetic floor is a property of THIS trainable set at THIS token count; a different active-expert count or sequence geometry moves every term in it. (2) IT SAYS NOTHING ABOUT WHETHER THE ARITHMETIC IS NECESSARY. 70.8 ms of measured GEMM and grouped-expert time is not a proof that those FLOPs must be issued. Fewer active experts, a cheaper attention, a sparser projection or a different algorithm all act inside the retained term and are untouched here. The bound says non-arithmetic treatments cannot reach the terminal; it does not say the arithmetic is irreducible. (3) PRECISION IS THE NAMED SURVIVING ROUTE AND IT IS NOT REFUTED. Cycle 17 refuted the 2x CONTRACTION-RATE premise at the one arm that has run, at 1.0597x and 1.2196x, and its own not_closed list keeps the route open: the contractions still BEAT bf16, the population beyond one projection site per geometry is unmeasured, the wrapper is unauthored and unsized, and FP16 accumulation carries the same published dense rate on Ada. What would settle it is a POPULATION-LEVEL contraction measurement across the 6.08 TF of linear work, which nothing has run. (4) THE PROFILED/GOVERNED TRANSFER IS AN ARGUMENT, NOT AN IDENTITY. The class unions come from a profiled capture and the step comes from a governed run. Cycle 18 justified the transfer for the UNION specifically -- 130,996.2 profiled against 131,055.6 governed, 0.05 percent -- and the SPAN does not transfer at all. If the union under instrumentation differed materially from the union without it, every term here moves. (5) THE ARITHMETIC/NON-ARITHMETIC SPLIT IS THE CLASS TABLE S. gemm_bf16 includes the cutlass memory-efficient attention kernels, and the nongemm bandwidth row already records that the attention class matched ZERO kernels in v2 because attention runs under names falling into gemm_bf16 or triton_fused. The overlap row is INCONCLUSIVE with every not_closed line standing, and the measured timeline has zero concurrency. If that overlap is unachievable the best case is 16.8 ms worse, not better. SUCCESSOR: measure the CONTRACTION speedup at the population level rather than at one projection site per geometry -- the one route the refuted cycles leave standing inside the retained 70.8 ms.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM. A speedup measured at one site per geometry is a property of that geometry. The population it would be applied to is not uniform in geometry: the leading dimension m of an aten::mm varies across the linear class, and the device time is distributed across those m very unevenly. So the question is not "what did FP8 achieve" but "at which m does the population s time actually sit, and did the arm measure there". THE FAILURE MODE THIS IS POINTED AT IS MINE. The natural next move after cycle 17 is to price the FP8 route by its best measured figure, 1.2196x, or by the mean of the two. Both are unweighted statistics over a sample of two, and if the better figure came from a geometry carrying almost none of the time, both overstate what the route can do to the step. Cycle 17 refused to quote a replacement step-level figure for exactly this reason; this cycle measures the thing that refusal was protecting. THE INSTRUMENT IS NEW AND IT REFUSES SIX WAYS. scripts/issue1945/fp8_population_weight.py joins the measured per-geometry ratios onto the population by the leading dimension m and refuses: a population whose enumerated sites do not reconstruct the class totals (POPULATION_INCOMPLETE -- a top-N table would understate the unmeasured share, in the flattering direction); a speedup weighted against a different capture than it was measured on (TRACE_MISMATCH); a ratio with no digest, run id or method (SPEEDUP_UNPROVENANCED); a measured geometry absent from the population (GEOMETRY_UNLOCATED); a non-positive ratio (SPEEDUP_NOT_POSITIVE); and, load-bearing here, any attempt to impute a ratio to a geometry the arm never ran (EXTRAPOLATION_ATTEMPTED). Unmeasured time is published as unmeasured, never interpolated. Its deliberate-red battery is scripts/issue1945/fp8_population_weight_reds.py: 8 cases, 0 failing, including two load-bearing GREENS, so the verdict comes from a function with more than one reachable outcome.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM. 24 forward and 24 backward kernel instances per step are not 24 repetitions of one call. The decoder issues attention per document, and documents within a 4x1024 batch need not present the same causal geometry to a block-causal kernel; the backward symbol itself carries seqaligned in its name. If the instances are heterogeneous, then the block s 3.805x time ratio is an average over a mixture, a treatment priced against it is priced against a call that may not exist, and the right unit of attack is a sub-population rather than the class. If they are homogeneous, the aggregate is trustworthy and the 3.805x is a property of every call -- which makes the FLOP-ratio gap a fact about the kernel rather than about the mixture. EITHER ANSWER IS USEFUL AND I DO NOT KNOW WHICH IT IS. Unlike cycles 17, 19 and 20, where I had already performed the arithmetic and said so at predict, this instrument has NOT been run against the real trace. Its deliberate-red battery is built entirely on SYNTHETIC traces for exactly that reason: running the battery proves the refusals without showing me the answer. THE INSTRUMENT REPORTS A DISTRIBUTION AND NOTHING ELSE. scripts/issue1945/attention_call_distribution.py takes every fmha_cutlassF and fmha_cutlassB kernel instance whose START falls inside a census_step window -- WHOLE, never clipped to the boundary, because clipping would manufacture precisely the spread under measurement -- and reports min, quartiles, median, max, max-over-median, q3-over-q1, top-quartile share, coefficient of variation, distinct symbols, and the per-window means. It is profile_strict_fp8_projection.py in the counterpart seat s worktree, bound by binding.json in custody cia-strict-fp8-profile-20260913T230000Z. It is an AUTHORING job and not a dispatch, on four independent grounds: it asserts binding[profile_shapes]==[256,4096]; it asserts m in (256,4096) and k==1024 and n==3072 at the operand check; it hashes its own file against binding[worker_sha256] so any edit invalidates its binding by construction; and it does not run the model at all -- it replays SAVED OPERANDS whose shapes are fixed at those two geometries. BUT READING IT SURFACED SOMETHING LARGER THAN THE ANSWER I WENT LOOKING FOR. The two measured sites are experts.0.layers.13.down.weight and experts.1.layers.23.down.weight -- EXPERT DOWN-PROJECTIONS, executed through the grouped row API native_api.rows, at k=1024 and n=3072. The m is the number of ROWS ROUTED TO ONE EXPERT, not an architectural dimension. CYCLE 20 WEIGHTED THOSE RATIOS BY THE aten::mm POPULATION of the captured training trace: 15 sites, 40,731.0 us/step, whose four m4096 members are [4096,1024]x[1024,2048], [4096,2048]x[2048,1024], [4096,1024]x[1024,1024] and [4096,1024]x[1024,32768]. NOT ONE POPULATION SITE CARRIES n=3072 OR k=3072, and the instrument proves that 15-site table is the COMPLETE mm population by reconstructing the by_mma_shape class totals within 1 us. So the shape the arm measured does not occur anywhere in the population its ratio was weighted by. A SCAN OF THE CAPTURED TRACE SHOWS 3072 IS PRESENT IN THE RUN but on other operators: aten::as_strided [[4,3072,1024]], AccumulateGrad [[3072,1024]], aten::mul [[4096,3072]], with cpu_ops _ResidentGroupedSwiGLU (72), DynamicGrouped (216), _DocumentReducedLinear (720) and aten::bmm (144) beside aten::mm (7,998). AND THE REGISTRY ALREADY NAMES THE CLASS. other-class-is-an-instrument-artifact-partition-restated-20260914 [COMPLETED] assigns _rows 11,510.0 + _weights 6,558.1 = 18,068.1 us/step to gemm_grouped_expert -- and _rows and _weights are EXACTLY the symbols fp8_wrapper_decomposition.py CONTRACTION_EXACT names as the arm s contraction.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM. fp8_wrapper_decomposition.py classifies a kernel as CONTRACTION by two disjoint rules: an EXACT name set (_rows, _weights, _fp8_rows, _fp8_weights -- the grouped-expert row API) and a PREFIX set (cutlass, sm80_xmma_gemm_, sm89_xmma_gemm_, ampere_, volta_ -- the dense kernels an aten::mm issues). Those two rules select DIFFERENT POPULATIONS. If the arm s traces contain only the EXACT group while the population cycle 20 weighted by is made of the PREFIX group, then cycle 20 joined a grouped-expert measurement to a dense-trunk population on the coincidence that both have a leading dimension that can equal 4096 -- in one case the number of rows routed to an expert, in the other the whole batch of 4 documents of 1024 positions. The numbers agree and the quantities do not. WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A CAVEAT. Cycle 20 s claim boundary discloses that the join keys on m only and that within one m the population carries several distinct N and K. If that is what the bytes say, then BOTH of cycle 20 s legs rest on the wrong denominator -- coverage 0.5750 was computed over a population the arm never ran on, and the time-weighted 1.0672x charged m4096 with 54.43 percent of a class the arm never touched -- and the registered successor is pointed at the wrong target, because m1024 in that table is a dense-trunk leading dimension and not a routed expert load. LEG 1, in the captured training trace: the union device time of the arm s EXACT symbols inside census_step windows, the union device time of kernels whose innermost enclosing cpu_op is aten::mm, and the union of the intersection of those two sets -- attribution by correlation first and by innermost containing cpu_op span second, the same rule other_class_symbol_census.py uses. The instrument therefore enumerates the mm population s COMPLETE symbol set: ten symbols, every one dense (ampere_bf16_s1688gemm, ampere_bf16_s16816gemm, cublasLt splitKreduce, ampere_sgemm, gemvx), and arm_symbols_present_in_mm_population is EMPTY. INSTRUMENT CHANGE DISCLOSED. The first implementation attributed each kernel by scanning every cpu_op span per query, which is O(kernels x ops) on 44,632 x 215,100 and did not finish; it was stopped and rewritten as a single interval sweep, and the membership rule was widened from INNERMOST enclosing cpu_op to ANY enclosing cpu_op. events.observation: Cycle 22 established that the FP8 arm s contraction kernels are the grouped-expert row API (_rows, _weights) and share ZERO microseconds with the aten::mm population cycle 20 weighted them by. That leaves the arm joined to the RIGHT class -- gemm_grouped_expert, 18,068.1 us/step -- and registered a successor: the routed-load distribution of that class, because the arm s geometry variable is the number of rows routed to a group and not a matrix dimension. QUERYING THE PROPOSITION IN ITS OWN VOCABULARY RETURNED A ROW THAT ANSWERS HALF OF IT ALREADY. `grouped expert rows calls per step` returns grouped-expert-path-achieved-compute-rate-20260914 [COMPLETED], whose site table records the production forward geometries as [4096,1024] x [4,1024,3072] at 3,842.7 us/step over 24 calls and [4096,3072] x [4,3072,1024] at 1,951.0 us/step over 12. The weight operand s FIRST DIMENSION IS THE GROUP COUNT, and it is 4. The row also records a row_block_padding_upper_bound of 0.0461 for the first site, which is exactly (4-1)*63/4096 -- so the group count is not my reading of a shape string, it is confirmed by a number that row computed independently. `expert load balance routing` and `routing distribution imbalance` return NO MATCH, and a filesystem search of the receipt trees for group_sizes, expert_counts, rows_per_expert, tokens_per_expert and assignment_counts returns nothing: the per-group ROW COUNTS of the production call are runtime data that exist in no artifact on disk. AND THE ARM S OWN RECEIPT RECORDS ITS GROUP PARTITION EXACTLY. result.json in custody cia-strict-fp8-profile-20260913T230000Z carries, beside each comparison s [M,K,N] shape, a `lengths` list: experts.1.layers.23.down.weight has lengths [256] -- ONE group -- and experts.0.layers.13.down.weight has [256] repeated SIXTEEN times. So the arm s m4096 site is not 4096 rows in 4 groups; it is 4096 rows in 16 groups of 256.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM. The grouped row kernel partitions the ROW dimension by cumulative offsets and rounds each group up to a 64-row block, so the hardware performs up to (G-1)*63/M more row-work than the useful count -- the bound the efficiency row records. G is therefore a real execution parameter of the call and not a labelling convention: at fixed M, K and N, a call with 16 groups runs a different tile decomposition, a different number of programs that exit early, and a different padding overhead from a call with 4. WHY IT MATTERS FOR THE SURVIVING ROUTE. The FP8 ratios 1.0597x at m4096 and 1.2196x at m256 are the only precision measurements this campaign holds, and after cycle 22 the only class they can lawfully be applied to is gemm_grouped_expert. Applying them requires that the arm ran the structure the class runs. If the arm s m4096 configuration is 16 groups against the production s 4, then the one arm geometry that matches a production site in [M,K,N] does not match it in the parameter that governs how the kernel decomposes the work -- and its padding upper bound is (16-1)*63/4096 = 0.2307 against the site s 0.0461, a factor of five more admissible waste. THE INSTRUMENT. scripts/issue1945/fp8_arm_group_structure.py reads the arm s `lengths` from its own result receipt and each production forward site s group count from the efficiency receipt s geometry string, joins them on (M,K,N), and reports for each pair whether the group counts agree within a factor of 2. It CROSS-CHECKS every inferred production group count against that site s independently recorded padding upper bound and REFUSES (PADDING_FORMULA_DISAGREES) if the two disagree, so no verdict rests on a group count read from a shape string alone. Backward sites are excluded because their recorded geometry does not carry the grouped weight operand. Refusals: NO_ARM_SITES, ARM_SITE_MISSING_LENGTHS, LENGTHS_SUM_MISMATCH, NO_CAPTURED_SITES, GEOMETRY_UNPARSEABLE, PADDING_FORMULA_DISAGREES. IT COMPOSES NOTHING. Whether a ratio measured at one group structure transfers to another is a question about the kernel, not about these two receipts, and this cycle does not answer it.

events.refuted_if: The arm REPRODUCES the production structure. events.hypothesis: WHY A JOIN DEFECT IS THE FAILURE THIS CAMPAIGN PRODUCES, mechanically rather than as a mood. A measurement is a number attached to conditions. events.observation: CYCLE 26 REFUTED THE JOIN HYPOTHESIS AND ITS SIXTH NOT_CLOSED LINE NAMES THIS ONE. An exhaustive enumeration of all 1,126 composed quantities in the campaign two append-only records found every one of the 20 flagged cross-provenance compositions DECLARED by its own row. That is a finding about the ROWS. It is not a finding about how those numbers are subsequently QUOTED, and cycle 26 recorded the gap in its own words: a well-conditioned join is still a join, the declaration means the number may not be quoted BARE, and this cycle did not look for it. THE ROWS DO NOT MERELY CONDITION, THEY PROHIBIT. Read across the registry, a recurring clause is an explicit refusal of a specific downstream use: "no absolute idle microsecond figure from this capture may be quoted as governed"; "never a measured ceiling and never an impossibility premise"; "expressing it against the 175,190 us governed step would compose across the profiled/governed boundary and is not quoted"; "nothing here may be quoted as an improvement or a ceiling under the governed-run evidence contract"; "not a prediction about the governed step and not a ceiling on the precision route"; "NO STEP-LEVEL ROUTE PRICE IS QUOTED"; "THE SPAN does not transfer at all". Each of those is a named number plus a named forbidden use. AND THE PROSE SURFACES ARE WHERE THE NUMBERS ARE ACTUALLY READ, not the registry. state/completion-push-ledger.md is roughly 10,878 CRLF lines and is the largest of them; state/now-next-after.md is the routing record; state/issue1945-receipts/*.md are the prose receipts. Every operator-facing line, every routing header and every receipt narrative draws its numbers from rows that fence them, and nothing has ever checked whether a fence survived the quotation. THE CAMPAIGN HAS ALREADY PAID FOR THIS CLASS ONCE, in the governing rule rather than in a row: the 1945-terminal-is-80k correction withdraws an impossibility sentence I wrote four lines above a clause forbidding exit-ramp language, and its own generalisation is that the shape "arrives as the last sentence of a correct derivation". That is a bare quotation of a conditioned number, caught by the counterpart seat and not by any instrument.

events.hypothesis: WHY THE QUOTING SURFACE IS WHERE THIS DEFECT WOULD LIVE, mechanically. A registry row is written at the moment of measurement, by the seat that just ran the instrument, with every limitation in working memory. A ledger block, a routing header or a chat line is written later, under compression, to say what changed. Compression is the mechanism: the number is the part that carries information and the fence is the part that costs words, so the fence is what a shorter sentence drops. Nothing in the pipeline re-reads the row. THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE AS EVERY DEFECT THIS CAMPAIGN HAS PRODUCED, one surface further out. A claim about the present sourced from a record of the past -- except here the record is correct and the QUOTATION of it is what drifts. The lock file, the gate D blocker, the stored count beside its enumeration, the Running clause with no process: in each case a true statement existed somewhere and the thing acted on was a lossy copy of it. WHY IT IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY A DEFECT TO QUOTE A NUMBER WITHOUT ITS CONDITION. Every summary is lossy by construction and a report that restated every fence would report nothing. So the hypothesis is NOT that conditions go unrestated. It is narrower and it is checkable: that a number whose row contains an EXPLICIT PROHIBITION on a specific use is, somewhere in the prose surfaces, used in exactly the prohibited way. A prohibition is not a caveat -- it names the use and forbids it, so violating it is a binary question with a text answer rather than a judgment about how much context is enough. THE MECHANISM OF THE INSTRUMENT: extract from every CURRENT registry row the prohibition clauses it states and the numeric literals each clause fences; then enumerate every occurrence of those literals in the prose surfaces; then, for each occurrence, read the window for the prohibited use and for any fence. Mechanical extraction, adjudication by reading -- the same division cycle 26 declared, and the same reason: a pattern can find a candidate and cannot rule one.

That is: every quotation of a prohibited-use number either carries the fence, or does not make the forbidden use. Also REFUTED if the enumeration cannot be made exhaustive -- if the instrument cannot show that it read every prose surface it names and every current row, it refuses rather than reporting zero, exactly as cycle 26 instrument does. SUPPORTED requires at least one occurrence, in a prose surface, of a number whose own registry row explicitly forbids that use, quoted in that use, with no fence in its window -- shown by quoting the prohibition and the violating sentence side by side. A SUPERSEDED OR ALREADY-CORRECTED QUOTATION DOES NOT COUNT. The ledger is append-only and carries its own corrections; a bare quotation later withdrawn in the same record is evidence the mechanism worked, not that it failed, and the instrument reports those separately. A QUOTATION BY THE ROW ITSELF DOES NOT COUNT either -- the prose receipt that STATES the prohibition necessarily contains both the number and the forbidden phrase in one window. NO TIMING CLAIM, NO NEW MEASUREMENT, NO CARD. The verdict is about the fidelity of this campaign quotations of its own record, adjudicated by reading both sides.

hypotheses.explanation: WHY THE QUOTING SURFACE IS WHERE THIS DEFECT WOULD LIVE, mechanically. A registry row is written at the moment of measurement, by the seat that just ran the instrument, with every limitation in working memory. A ledger block, a routing header or a chat line is written later, under compression, to say what changed. Compression is the mechanism: the number is the part that carries information and the fence is the part that costs words, so the fence is what a shorter sentence drops. Nothing in the pipeline re-reads the row. THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE AS EVERY DEFECT THIS CAMPAIGN HAS PRODUCED, one surface further out. A claim about the present sourced from a record of the past -- except here the record is correct and the QUOTATION of it is what drifts. The lock file, the gate D blocker, the stored count beside its enumeration, the Running clause with no process: in each case a true statement existed somewhere and the thing acted on was a lossy copy of it. WHY IT IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY A DEFECT TO QUOTE A NUMBER WITHOUT ITS CONDITION. Every summary is lossy by construction and a report that restated every fence would report nothing. So the hypothesis is NOT that conditions go unrestated. It is narrower and it is checkable: that a number whose row contains an EXPLICIT PROHIBITION on a specific use is, somewhere in the prose surfaces, used in exactly the prohibited way. A prohibition is not a caveat -- it names the use and forbids it, so violating it is a binary question with a text answer rather than a judgment about how much context is enough. THE MECHANISM OF THE INSTRUMENT: extract from every CURRENT registry row the prohibition clauses it states and the numeric literals each clause fences; then enumerate every occurrence of those literals in the prose surfaces; then, for each occurrence, read the window for the prohibited use and for any fence. Mechanical extraction, adjudication by reading -- the same division cycle 26 declared, and the same reason: a pattern can find a candidate and cannot rule one.

That is: every quotation of a prohibited-use number either carries the fence, or does not make the forbidden use. Also REFUTED if the enumeration cannot be made exhaustive -- if the instrument cannot show that it read every prose surface it names and every current row, it refuses rather than reporting zero, exactly as cycle 26 instrument does. SUPPORTED requires at least one occurrence, in a prose surface, of a number whose own registry row explicitly forbids that use, quoted in that use, with no fence in its window -- shown by quoting the prohibition and the violating sentence side by side. A SUPERSEDED OR ALREADY-CORRECTED QUOTATION DOES NOT COUNT. The ledger is append-only and carries its own corrections; a bare quotation later withdrawn in the same record is evidence the mechanism worked, not that it failed, and the instrument reports those separately. A QUOTATION BY THE ROW ITSELF DOES NOT COUNT either -- the prose receipt that STATES the prohibition necessarily contains both the number and the forbidden phrase in one window. NO TIMING CLAIM, NO NEW MEASUREMENT, NO CARD. The verdict is about the fidelity of this campaign quotations of its own record, adjudicated by reading both sides.

events.observation: THE PRODUCTION GROUPED LAUNCHER RUNS FOUR TIMES THE PROGRAMS OF THE ONLY ARM EVER MEASURED, AND NOTHING HAS PRICED THE DIFFERENCE. Cycle 25 corrected the arm-side join and registered exactly this as an open, unpriced question in its own not_closed list: "the row kernel grid dim0 is cdiv(m,64) over the FULL row count for EVERY group, so at G=4 three quarters of the programs exist only to hit the early exit `if first < end:`. Sizing dim0 per group is a source-derived candidate treatment never before named. An empty program costs a scheduling slot, not a matmul, and NOTHING HERE MEASURES WHAT THAT SLOT COSTS. No ceiling, no sign, no arm." THE CORRECTED JOIN, from that cycle: at the production forward site [4096,1024] x [4,1024,3072], 3,842.7 us/step, the arm at G=1 launched 1,536 programs and all 1,536 worked, zero empty; production at G=4 launches 6,144 programs, the same 1,536 units of work, 4,608 empty. The arm launched 0.25x of production. READ AT SOURCE THIS TURN, in the same worktree the arm imported (src/ember/model/ember_v0_grouped_capture.py): rows() launches _rows on grid (cdiv(m,64), cdiv(n,128), groups) and the kernel opens with `group = tl.program_id(2); start = tl.load(O + group - 1, group > 0, other=0); end = tl.load(O + group); first = start + tl.program_id(0) * BM; if first < end:` -- so dim0 is sized by the whole row count and every group re-walks it. The backward weight kernel _weights launches on (cdiv(k,64), cdiv(n,128), b.shape[0]) and stores to `W + group * K * N + ...` into a db allocated at b.shape, so its OUTPUT is [G,K,N]: at G=1 the arm wrote a quarter of the weight-gradient bytes production writes. Also derivable and also never measured. WHY THIS BLOCKS THE FP8 QUESTION RATHER THAN SITTING BESIDE IT. The only FP8 ratio this campaign holds -- 1.0597x at the kernel level, plus forward 0.796 and dX 0.629 -- is a ratio against a BF16 native that ran at G=1. If the BF16 denominator itself moves at G=4, that ratio moves for a reason that has nothing to do with FP8, and no FP8 arm at the production partition can be read until the BF16 geometry term is known. Structural coverage of the grouped-expert class is 0.0 us/step of 18,068.1 either way.

events.hypothesis: THE EXPLANATION UNDER TEST is the one implicit in every reading of the 1.0597x ratio to date: that the group axis is a scheduling detail and an early-exit program is free, so the same arithmetic costs the same whether it is launched as one group of 4,096 rows or four groups of 1,024. On that account the 4,608 empty programs cost only their scheduling slots, the SMs retire them in the launch tail, and G=4 and G=1 are the same measurement. THE MECHANISM THAT WOULD MAKE IT FALSE is equally concrete. An empty program is not free: it is scheduled onto an SM, reads two int32 values from the offsets vector, evaluates a predicate and retires. At G=4 on this site that is 4,608 such programs against 1,536 real ones, a 4x occupancy of the launch queue for 1x of the work, and the row kernel is a short-lived tile kernel where per-program overhead is a large fraction of per-program work. The backward is a second and independent mechanism in the same direction: dW at G=4 writes four [K,N] slabs where G=1 writes one, which is 4x the store traffic and 4x the grid on the group axis for the same accumulated rows. WHY THE ARITHMETIC IS IDENTICAL AND THE COMPARISON THEREFORE CLEAN. The saved operand carries ONE weight of [1024,3072] and 4,096 rows of one expert. Replicating that weight across four group slabs gives every row the same weight it had at G=1, so the forward and dX results at G=4 must be BITWISE IDENTICAL to G=1: the offsets 1024/2048/3072/4096 are all multiples of BM=64, so the row tiles are the same tiles and the K loop runs in the same order; only which program computes which tile changes. That makes bit-identity a precondition the run checks rather than a result it reports, and it means any timing difference is attributable to launcher geometry alone. dW is deliberately NOT bit-identical -- at G=4 it is four per-group slabs whose sum is the G=1 slab up to BF16 rounding boundaries -- which is exactly the production shape, so dW is measured but is not under the identity check. THIS IS A MEASUREMENT-VALIDITY REPAIR, NOT A TREATMENT ARM, and its pre-run ceiling says so: it has NO ceiling on the governed number, it removes no milliseconds, and it is refused by the 1.5x bar of 1945-multiplicative-movement-only if read as a treatment. What it buys is (a) the first measurement of the grouped-expert class at the group structure production actually runs, where coverage is 0.0 of 18,068.1 us/step, and (b) the price of the empty-program slot, which cycle 25 registered as a candidate treatment with no ceiling, no sign and no arm. A sign and a magnitude here are what would let that candidate be named at all.

These have their own G=1-versus-G=1 floors and their own numbers; the criterion above is the FORWARD alone, because the forward is the term the 1.0597x ratio's denominator is built from and a single criterion that fuses three kernels cannot be refuted cleanly. events.hypothesis: WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE, and the one thing in it that corrected a reading of mine before the reading reached an artifact. (1) THE dW RESULT WAS CONFOUNDED AND THE CONFOUND WAS DECISIVE. The arm measured dW at both group counts as a declared-but-not-criterion leg and found G=4 FASTER by 11.399 us (175.512 against 186.911, ratio 0.93901, floor 0.327), despite writing four [1024,3072] slabs against one. My working mechanism reading was occupancy: the G=1 _weights grid (16,24,1) is 384 programs on a 128-SM card against G=4's 1,536. A second leg run under the same window refutes it. NC -- the per-group chunk count, a kernel constexpr -- moved with G in the arm: 16 at G=1 against 4 at G=4. A 2x2 over G in {1,4} and NC in {4,16} separates them: g1_nc16 190.614, g1_nc4 166.359, g4_nc4 174.592, g4_nc16 212.451 us. The GRID term is POSITIVE in both directions (+8.233 us at NC=4, +21.837 us at NC=16): holding chunking fixed, MORE groups costs MORE, which is the direction the extra output bytes predict and the opposite of the occupancy reading. The whole apparent win is the CHUNK-LOOP term (-24.255 us at G=1, -37.859 us at G=4): fewer, larger chunks are faster. The interaction is -13.604 us, comparable to the terms themselves, so the two do not separate additively and the receipt says so rather than hiding it. The consequence that matters: at MATCHED chunking, production (g4_nc4, 174.592) is SLOWER than one group (g1_nc4, 166.359) by 8.233 us on dW. The empty program is free on the forward and is NOT free on the backward weight kernel. Receipt: state/issue1945-receipts/grouped-launcher-dw-decomposition-20260915T0225Z.json. (2) dX IS NOT FREE EITHER, and it was never confounded: +0.551 us at G=4 against a 0.327 us floor, ratio 1.00337. Real, +0.34%, and small. (3) THE FP8 HALF IS UNMEASURED. This cycle establishes only that the BF16 denominator transfers on the forward. The registered cycle-25 successor is the FP8 arm at four groups of 1,024 rows, and it still needs a new self-binding worker: the existing one (run ac58938b, worker profile_strict_fp8_projection.py) asserts its own sha256 against its binding.json and cannot be edited, and its line 153 hardcodes offsets=torch.tensor([m]) -- G=1. (4) ONE REPLICATED WEIGHT, NOT FOUR PRODUCTION WEIGHTS. Every group contracted against the same [1024,3072] slab, replicated with .repeat() into four distinct slabs rather than an expand view so no cache line is shared. events.hypothesis: MECHANISM: the wrapper's cost scales with activation BYTES while the contraction's saving scales with FLOPs, and at these shapes the byte term wins. The per-tensor amax is a reduction over the WHOLE activation executed as two unfused kernels -- an elementwise abs that reads the activation and writes a same-sized temporary, then a reduction that reads that temporary -- so it moves roughly three activation-sized buffers through DRAM per quantized tensor and is bandwidth-bound end to end. The contraction it enables is compute-bound, and its measured saving is small: 1875.145 against 1987.038 us is a ratio of 0.9437, only 5.6 percent, not the 2x the format's tensor rate suggests. So a fixed bandwidth tax is being paid to buy a small percentage of a compute term. TWO CONSEQUENCES THAT FOLLOW FROM THE MECHANISM RATHER THAN FROM THE ARITHMETIC. First, the tax is GROUP-INDEPENDENT: a per-tensor amax over the whole activation does not care how the rows are partitioned, so G can only move the contraction term, and a grouped FP8 path cannot reduce the wrapper at all. Second, the tax is SHAPE-DEPENDENT in the opposite direction to the saving: at m256 the same decomposition gives BF16 305.984 against FP8 466.117 = 250.884 contraction + 215.233 wrapper, so the wrapper is 46 percent of the candidate at the small shape against 24 percent at m4096 -- the arithmetic intensity falls and the tax grows as a share.
