events.hypothesis: MECHANISM. An elementwise kernel whose operands were just written by the preceding kernel, and whose per-invocation working set fits in the 72 MB L2, can be served entirely from L2; its traffic never reaches DRAM and its achieved figure is an L2 rate, not a DRAM rate. That is the only reading consistent with an aggregate ABOVE the published DRAM number, short of the byte estimate being wrong -- and the byte estimate is a lower bound, which biases the achieved rate DOWN, so the excess is if anything understated. WHY IT SELECTS A ROUTE RATHER THAN DESCRIBING ONE. Fusion that keeps intermediates in registers is priced by what the intermediates currently cost. If they cost a DRAM round trip, the byte-reduction direction is worth something near the 25.2 ms the elementwise row left open. If they cost an L2 round trip, the same fusion saves L2 traffic at a fraction of the price per byte, and the 25.2 ms is not available. Two opposite valuations of the same treatment, decided by one property of the data, and nothing on disk has measured it.

events.refuted_if: MORE THAN 50 PERCENT of the elementwise class's sized device time is spent in kernel invocations whose per-invocation working set EXCEEDS 72 MB. Such an invocation cannot be L2-resident by capacity alone, so if the bulk of the class sits there, the class genuinely touches DRAM, the aggregate excess is an artifact of a minority of small kernels, and the byte-reduction direction survives at something near its stated size.
events.supported_if: 50 PERCENT OR MORE of the class's sized device time is spent in invocations whose per-invocation working set is at or below 72 MB, i.e. L2-resident-CAPABLE. That would make the headline 1,160.6 GB/s an L2 rate for the bulk of the class and would price byte-reduction fusion against L2 bandwidth rather than DRAM bandwidth. CAPABILITY IS NOT RESIDENCY and the ruling says so: fitting in 72 MB is necessary, not sufficient, because L2 is shared across the whole step and eviction between two consumers of the same buffer is invisible to this trace.
events.instrument: A bucketing pass over the elementwise population of an on-disk captured trace, reusing the join and the byte derivation of scripts/issue1945/captured_elementwise_bandwidth.py: for each sized elementwise kernel, compute the per-invocation working-set bytes already derived there, bucket its device time by that figure against the 72 MB L2 capacity, and report the time share on each side plus the distribution. Analysis-only: no GPU, no lease, no new capture. NOTE OF RECORD -- the trace the 1,160.6 GB/s figure came from (cia-captured-trace-20260914T172624Z.json) is no longer on disk; this runs against cia-captured-trace-20260914T182441Z.json, a DIFFERENT capture. The class totals may therefore differ from the source receipt, and whether the aggregate rate reproduces at all on an independent capture is a second, unplanned reading this run produces.

events.because: The frozen criterion was: REFUTED IF more than 50 percent of the elementwise class's sized device time is spent in kernel invocations whose per-invocation working set EXCEEDS 72 MB. It is 12.88 percent, across 9 kernels per step, at sized coverage 0.996. The criterion is not met, so the reading is SUPPORTED exactly as frozen. AND THE MECHANISM THE HYPOTHESIS PROPOSED IS REFUSED BY THE SAME DATA, which is reported here rather than left in the receipt. The explanation offered was that the above-DRAM aggregate is an L2 effect. If it were, the population that CANNOT be L2-resident by capacity would sit at or below the 1008 GB/s reference. It sits furthest above it: exceeds-L2 achieves 1390.9 GB/s against fits-L2 at 1146.8, and the >256MB bucket 1560.3. The likelier cause is an instrument property, not a cache one -- the byte model charges every sized input read once plus the largest written once, which over-counts aten::fill_ two-for-one and aten::copy_ three-for-two, and those two sites are 2,408.6 of the 3,522.1 us in the exceeding bucket. So the capacity question is answered and the residency question is not, and the aggregate excess over the published reference is at least partly an artifact of the byte model.

events.hypothesis: WHAT THE REFUTED MECHANISM DOES NOT CLOSE. (a) L2 RESIDENCY IS STILL UNMEASURED. The elementwise row's not_closed line stands untouched: capacity is necessary and not sufficient, nothing here reads a cache counter, and 87 percent of class time being L2-resident-CAPABLE says nothing about whether a buffer survived between its producer and its consumer. What changed is that the above-DRAM aggregate is no longer usable as indirect evidence for residency, because the non-resident population exceeds the reference by more. (b) THE BYTE MODEL IS NOW THE LOAD-BEARING SUSPECT AND IS ITSELF UNMEASURED. Both this receipt and the one it extends derive bytes from recorded input dims, and the over-count is now known to be large enough to matter at the top of the distribution. A measured DRAM-traffic counter would settle it and this build has none. (c) THE BYTE-REDUCTION DIRECTION IS NEITHER CONFIRMED NOR REFUTED. It was the reason this cycle ran; the cycle failed to price it, because pricing it needs the residency answer the mechanism failure just removed the shortcut to. THE UNPLANNED FINDING, which is the cycle's real product: the class is BIMODAL. 1,844 of 3,336 sized kernels per step have working sets at or under 1 MB and take 2,269.4 us -- 8.3 percent of class time -- at 29.4 GB/s, 2.9 percent of the reference. Kernels between 8 MB and 72 MB are 1,004 per step and take 20,519.7 us, 75.1 percent of class time, at 1,202-1,261 GB/s. The bandwidth-bound ruling describes the second population and not the first. The small tail is the launch/occupancy population the row-1 framing was about, and it is 2,269.4 us: 1.4 percent of a 163,760 us governed step, far below the 1.5x arm bar, so it names which milliseconds belong to which story rather than nominating an arm. INSTRUMENT DEFECT FOUND AND CURED IN-CYCLE. The first run returned every kernel unsized -- that capture was taken without record_shapes -- and the script printed SUPPORTED, because an empty sized population makes the exceeding share 0.0 and the "more than 50 percent" criterion reads as unsatisfied. A verdict from an empty denominator is the persistent-lock-file defect inside a measurement. A coverage floor now refuses below 0.50 and names the cause; the refusal is receipted at elementwise-l2-residency-REFUSAL-20260915T0332Z.json, exit 2.

events.observation: THE OPERATOR OBJECTED THAT THE NUMBER HAS NOT MOVED IN TWELVE HOURS AND HE IS RIGHT. Gate A stands at 23,380.183126331838 of 80,000 applied positions/s, last moved by the 13:52Z gate B verdict. nvidia-smi reads 1325 MiB / 7 percent: the card is idle and no arm has been dispatched in that window. Everything landed since was measurement custody (PR 2289) or analysis-only loop cycles. Under gpu-never-idle rule 3 an idle GPU with a DISPATCHABLE arm is a defect of the seat, so the question this cycle exists to settle is whether a dispatchable arm exists at all. WHAT THE RECEIPTS SAY WHEN ASSEMBLED, which none of them says alone. (1) rows-1-and-3-candidate-20260914.md section 5 refuses rows 1 and 3, separately and stacked, at 1.25x against the 1.5x bar -- the whole of the device idle is 32,700 us of a 163,760 us step. (2) Its section 6b measures the linear GEMM class at 158.9 TF/s on s1688 (96.2 percent of the published dense bf16 rate) and 117.0 on s16816, so there is no bf16 kernel-quality win at those sites. (3) the-2x-fp8-tensor-rate-premise-is-not-observed-at-either-measured-site-20260914 then REFUTES the premise the FP8 half of the stack was priced on: measured contraction speedup is 1.0597x at m4096 and 1.2196x at m256 against the 2.0 assumed, and end to end the arm is SLOWER (0.8071x, 0.6565x) because the wrapper -- 59.1 percent of which is an unfused amax -- exceeds the contraction saving at both geometries. That row names its own successor in its last not_closed line: re-rule the selection so the non-GEMM half leads. This cycle is that act. (4) What survives is exactly one combination above the bar, and it has never been authored: the whole elementwise/norm population removed as DEVICE TIME (27,500 us -- explicitly left open by row 1 not_closed line (a), which refuted row 1 only as an IDLE-removal arm) stacked with all device idle (32,700 us). 60,200 us removed leaves 0.1036 s, which is 1.58x.

events.hypothesis: THE CLAIM UNDER TEST IS ABOUT THE ROUTE SET, NOT ABOUT A MECHANISM: that the non-GEMM stack is the ONLY treatment combination on this campaign whose pre-stated ceiling clears 1945-multiplicative-movement-only clause 1, AND that its ceiling at perfect effectiveness still lands far short of the 80,000 terminal. Both halves matter and they point opposite ways, which is why they are tested together rather than separately. The first half says an arm is dispatchable, so the card being idle is a defect with a cure. The second half says that arm, even if it collected every microsecond it aims at, produces about 36,940 positions/s and not 80,000 -- because 0.1036 s is still 2.02x the 0.0512 s the terminal allows, and what remains inside it is 78.6 ms of GEMM and attention arithmetic already running at 91 to 96 percent of the card published bf16 rate. WHY THIS IS NOT AN IMPOSSIBILITY CLAIM AND MAY NOT BE READ AS ONE (deterministic-closeable-units clause 3, 1945-terminal-is-80k clause 4): it prices the routes that have been MEASURED. It does not price FP16 accumulation, which carries the same published dense rate on Ada and which this campaign has never measured; it does not price an FP8 path with a fused or delayed-scaling encoder, which the wrapper decomposition names and nothing has measured; it does not price fewer FLOPs per position; and it does not price positions per optimizer step, which is a CONTRACT change and the operator to rule, priced at about 1.1x because only the 16.4 ms optimizer is genuinely fixed per step. The terminal is unchanged at 80,000. Measurement selects the ROUTE, never the exit.

events.refuted_if: REFUTED IF a treatment combination is found, from receipts already on disk at head 20338ddc, whose pre-stated ceiling against the 0.16376 s governed step is at or above 1.5x and which is NOT the non-GEMM stack (elementwise device time plus all device idle) -- OR if the non-GEMM stack own ceiling, recomputed from the measured class sizes, is at or above the 0.0512 s terminal, i.e. reaches 80,000. Either finding refutes this cycle.
events.supported_if: SUPPORTED IF the enumeration over every measured class at this head returns exactly one above-bar combination, the non-GEMM stack, AND its perfect-effectiveness step of 0.1036 s corresponds to about 36,940 positions/s, short of the terminal.
events.instrument: Analysis-only, no card, no lease: an enumeration over the measured class table in rows-1-and-3-candidate-20260914.md sections 5, 6, 6a and 6b, cross-checked against every registry row carrying a ceiling, computing each single lever and each pairwise and three-way stack against the 0.16376 s step with contending ceilings netted rather than summed.

events.because: The frozen criterion was: REFUTED IF a treatment combination is found whose ceiling is at or above 1.5x and which is NOT the non-GEMM stack, OR if the non-GEMM stack reaches the terminal. The enumeration returns TWO combinations at or above the bar, not one, so the first clause fires and the ruling is REFUTED. AND THE REFUTATION IS OF MY CRITERION, NOT OF THE ROUTE-SET FINDING, which is stated here rather than buried. The second above-bar entry is [all_device_idle, elementwise_class_as_device_time, fp8_at_every_mm_site] at 1.5813x -- numerically identical to the first, because fp8_at_every_mm_site enters the enumeration at ZERO microseconds after its 2.0x premise was refuted. It is the same treatment with a zero-valued lever appended, so the criterion counted SET MEMBERS where it meant DISTINCT TREATMENTS. That is a defect in how I wrote the falsifier, and it fired exactly as a falsifier should: I do not get to notice it after the numbers arrive and read the result as SUPPORTED instead. The criterion was not amended. WHAT THE ENUMERATION ACTUALLY SHOWS, unchanged by the ruling: the non-GEMM stack is 1.5813x, step 0.16376 -> 0.1036 s, about 36,971 positions/s if perfectly effective. NOTHING in the enumeration reaches the 0.0512 s terminal -- zero combinations of every measured lever, including the highest raw arithmetic at 1.8703x (idle plus elementwise plus the fused optimizer removed entirely), which is itself not admitted because removing the optimizer removes launches and therefore double-counts idle it would also remove.

events.hypothesis: WHAT THIS REFUTATION DOES NOT CLOSE. (a) THE ROUTE-SET FINDING SURVIVES INTACT. Both substantive halves hold: the non-GEMM stack is the only DISTINCT treatment above the 1.5x bar in the measured set, and no combination of measured levers reaches the terminal. What failed is a counting rule, and the successor restates it over distinct nonzero levers. (b) THE ENUMERATION IS OVER MEASURED LEVERS ONLY, so "only one clears the bar" is a statement about what has been measured and never about what is possible. Four routes sit outside it, unpriced because nothing has measured them: FP16 accumulation at the same published dense rate on Ada; an FP8 path with a fused or delayed-scaling encoder, which the wrapper decomposition names and nobody has built; fewer FLOPs per position; and positions per optimizer step, a CONTRACT change the operator rules, priced at about 1.1x. (c) IT IS NOT AN IMPOSSIBILITY CLAIM and may not be read as one. Impossibility on this target is rulable only by the operator from receipts; the terminal is unchanged at 80,000 and measurement selects the ROUTE, never the exit. (d) THE STACK IS UNAUTHORED. That a per-layer fused elementwise/norm kernel plus a whole-step graph with the optimizer inside would collect 60,200 us is the premise being priced, not a result; both halves are unbuilt and neither has a falsifier registered. (e) ONE HEAD, ONE GEOMETRY, ONE PROFILED CAPTURE, NO MATCHED-RUN VARIATION, so no figure here is quotable as an improvement or a measured ceiling under the governed-run evidence contract. THE OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE, which is why this cycle was run at all: the card has been idle for twelve hours and the operator is right to object. This cycle establishes that the idleness is NOT because no arm exists -- one does, at 1.58x -- so gpu-never-idle rule 3 stands as a defect with a named cure, and the cure is to build the non-GEMM stack. It also establishes that building it lands near 37,000 and not at 80,000, which is a fact the operator needs before he spends any more of the campaign on it, and which is his to rule on rather than mine.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM: the residency ordering cycle 30 measured is an artifact of the byte model, not of the cache. The correction acts on the exceeding-L2 side far harder than on the fitting side for two independent reasons that compound. First the RATE: the mis-charged ops carry 68 percent of the exceeding bucket time, so removing their inflation cuts that side numerator disproportionately. Second the MEMBERSHIP: the corrected working set of a fill_ is one buffer rather than two and of a copy_ is two rather than three, so sites near the 72 MB boundary MOVE from the exceeding side to the fitting side, and they take their inflated rate with them. Under the corrected model the ordering should invert -- fitting at or above exceeding -- which is what residency predicts and what cycle 30 did not see. WHY THIS DECIDES THE CAMPAIGN SELECTION AND NOT MERELY A PAST VERDICT. Cycle 31 established that exactly one distinct treatment clears the 1.5x arm bar, and its larger half is the whole elementwise class removed as device time, 27,500 us. Whether those microseconds are collectable depends on what sets them. If the class time is bytes that must cross DRAM regardless, fusion removes launches and intermediates but not traffic and the lever is far smaller than its class size. AND THE MARGIN IS 11.3 GB/s ON FIGURES NEAR 1070, ABOUT 1.05 PERCENT, WITH NO BETWEEN-RUN FLOOR AND NO MATCHED-RUN VARIATION. A one-percent inversion from a two-op correction to an estimated byte model is not a measurement of the cache. What the verdict licenses is narrow and is stated as such: cycle 30 refused the residency mechanism BECAUSE the ordering ran the wrong way, and that reason does not survive the correction. HALF OF MY OWN PREDICTED MECHANISM IS REFUTED INSIDE THIS SUPPORTED VERDICT AND IS RECORDED RATHER THAN ABSORBED. The explain stage named two compounding effects, rate and membership. MEMBERSHIP DID ESSENTIALLY NOTHING: exactly one kernel changed side, aten::fill_ [32768,1024] at 52.3 us/step, 0.19 percent of sized class time. The inversion is the rate half alone. events.hypothesis: MECHANISM: the class contains a LAUNCH-BOUND TAIL whose device time is set by per-kernel cost rather than by traffic, and a STREAMING BODY whose time is set by bytes. A fusion treatment removes per-kernel overhead and does not remove bytes, so it can collect the tail and not the body, and the honest lever is the tail rather than the class. HOW THE TWO ARE SEPARATED, per kernel rather than by eye: compare measured device time against the time that kernel corrected bytes would take at the published reference, and call the positive difference UNEXPLAINED BY BYTES. Summed over the class that is the ceiling on what a treatment can remove while leaving traffic unchanged. THE MECHANISM PREMISE IS STATED SEPARATELY FROM THE ARITHMETIC AND IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF. That fusion removes per-kernel overhead and no bytes is a claim about what the treatment DOES; it is not measured by this cycle, and the division is meaningless without it. Nothing here refutes it and nothing here sizes it." -- and nongemm-launch-consolidation-bound-is-3.9ms-not-55ms-20260914 [REFUTED] -- "(a) THE BYTE-REDUCTION DIRECTION IS UNTOUCHED and is where the ~40.6 ms lives". So the line is confirmed open by the newest evidence rather than merely unrefuted by the oldest. THE OBSERVATION. Cycle 34 priced the half of fusion that removes LAUNCHES at 7,017.0 us per step of the class 27,447.4, and that put cycle 31 only above-bar arm at 1.3202x. events.hypothesis: MECHANISM: the elementwise class device time is spent on two kinds of bytes. Some cross memory because a value has to REACH memory -- a residual stream, a checkpointed activation, anything a later consumer reads after other work intervenes. The rest crosses memory only because the value was materialised between two adjacent operations that could have passed it in registers. The second kind is ELIMINABLE, and eliminating it removes the traffic itself rather than the launch around it. HOW THE ELIMINABLE PART IS COUNTED, per kernel and from op identity rather than by eye. Pure MOVEMENT ops -- aten::copy_, aten::fill_, aten::zero_ -- perform no arithmetic, so a producer writing straight into the destination makes the whole kernel disappear, every traversal of it. Every other elementwise op keeps its arithmetic and can shed AT MOST ONE traversal of its largest tensor: the single crossing of the intermediate it produces or consumes. One traversal per kernel is deliberate -- each eliminated intermediate is charged exactly once, to one side of the edge, so a fused chain cannot be counted twice. THE TWO HALVES CONTEND AND ARE NOT SUMMED. A kernel removed by fusion loses its launch overhead AND its bytes, and those are the same milliseconds. So the composite is computed per kernel as min(duration, overhead_excess + eliminable_byte_time), never as the sum of the two class totals. Cycle 34 number and this one would otherwise double-count every kernel the treatment removes outright. THE MECHANISM PREMISE, STATED SEPARATELY FROM THE ARITHMETIC BECAUSE IT IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF AND IT IS WHERE MY OWN RECORD SAYS I FAIL: this counts what MAXIMAL fusion could reach -- every intermediate held in registers, every pure copy absorbed. It is an UPPER bound and it is not a claim that any implementable kernel reaches it. Register and shared-memory capacity, the residual stream, recompute boundaries and the autograd tape all force some intermediates to memory, and none of those constraints is measured here.

Cycle 34 measured the launch-only reading of that half at 7,017.0 and the arm fell to 1.3202x. This cycle asks the same question of the MAXIMAL reading, which is the most favourable number the class can produce. REFUTED IF the combined per-kernel capped removal -- overhead excess plus eliminable byte time, capped at each kernel measured duration -- is AT OR ABOVE 21,886.7 us per step on trace cia-captured-trace-20260914T183257Z.json. That would mean intermediate elimination does reach the bar, cycle 34 verdict was an artifact of pricing only the launch half, and the campaign DOES still have a measured arm above the operator bar.

events.because: SUPPORTED, and NARROWLY, which is stated first because the margin is the finding. THE FROZEN CRITERION: "REFUTED IF the combined per-kernel capped removal -- overhead excess plus eliminable byte time, capped at each kernel measured duration -- is AT OR ABOVE 21,886.7 us per step". MEASURED: 19,105.6 us. Below the threshold, so not refuted, but by 2,781.1 us -- 12.7 percent of the contribution the bar needs. The arm reaches 1.4627x against a 1.5x bar. THE TWO HALVES, AND THE DOUBLE COUNT THE CAP REMOVED. Launch overhead 7,017.0 us (cycle 34, recomputed here and identical, which is the check that the two instruments agree). Eliminable byte time 13,703.8 us -- 47.1 percent of the class corrected bytes. Their naive sum is 20,720.8; the per-kernel cap removes 1,615.2 us of double counting and gives 19,105.6. Summing the two class totals would have credited the same microseconds twice for the 1,172.3 kernels per step the treatment removes outright, and would have reported 20,720.8 -- still below the threshold, so the cap does not change the verdict, but it changes the number and it is published so the arithmetic is checkable rather than asserted. THE CLEAN SUB-LEVER, which is the most actionable thing here. Pure movement -- copy_, fill_, zero_, clone, contiguous, _to_copy -- is 784 kernels per step carrying 7,131.1 us at 775.9 GB/s, and it is removable IN FULL by construction, because those kernels compute nothing. The arithmetic remainder is 2,663 kernels, 20,316.2 us at 1172.3 GB/s, of which 11,974.4 us is removable under maximal fusion. WHY SUPPORTED IS THE RIGHT VERDICT AND NOT INCONCLUSIVE, given how close it is. The criterion was frozen before the run and the measurement is on the favourable side of every judgement call in the instrument: MAXIMAL fusion with every intermediate assumed fusible, every pure movement op assumed absorbable, and the receipt own contention note says the stack figure is an OVER-estimate because removing per-kernel overhead also removes inter-kernel gaps already counted in the 32,700 us idle lever. The true figure is below 1.4627x, not above it. A run that lands below its threshold on the most generous possible reading discriminated; it was not inconclusive.

hypotheses.explanation: MECHANISM: the elementwise class device time is spent on two kinds of bytes. Some cross memory because a value has to REACH memory -- a residual stream, a checkpointed activation, anything a later consumer reads after other work intervenes. The rest crosses memory only because the value was materialised between two adjacent operations that could have passed it in registers. The second kind is ELIMINABLE, and eliminating it removes the traffic itself rather than the launch around it. HOW THE ELIMINABLE PART IS COUNTED, per kernel and from op identity rather than by eye. Pure MOVEMENT ops -- aten::copy_, aten::fill_, aten::zero_ -- perform no arithmetic, so a producer writing straight into the destination makes the whole kernel disappear, every traversal of it. Every other elementwise op keeps its arithmetic and can shed AT MOST ONE traversal of its largest tensor: the single crossing of the intermediate it produces or consumes. One traversal per kernel is deliberate -- each eliminated intermediate is charged exactly once, to one side of the edge, so a fused chain cannot be counted twice. THE TWO HALVES CONTEND AND ARE NOT SUMMED. A kernel removed by fusion loses its launch overhead AND its bytes, and those are the same milliseconds. So the composite is computed per kernel as min(duration, overhead_excess + eliminable_byte_time), never as the sum of the two class totals. Cycle 34 number and this one would otherwise double-count every kernel the treatment removes outright. THE MECHANISM PREMISE, STATED SEPARATELY FROM THE ARITHMETIC BECAUSE IT IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF AND IT IS WHERE MY OWN RECORD SAYS I FAIL: this counts what MAXIMAL fusion could reach -- every intermediate held in registers, every pure copy absorbed. It is an UPPER bound and it is not a claim that any implementable kernel reaches it. Register and shared-memory capacity, the residual stream, recompute boundaries and the autograd tape all force some intermediates to memory, and none of those constraints is measured here.

events.observation: THE OBSERVATION, from cycle 35 own receipt rather than from a plan. The best stack this campaign has priced is exactly TWO levers -- all device idle at 32,700 us and maximal elementwise fusion with bytes included at 19,105.6 us -- and it reaches 1.4627x against the operator 1.5x bar. It is short by 2,781.1 us, which is 12.7 percent of the contribution the bar needs and 1.7 percent of the governed step. Every prior cycle read as "no arm is close"; this one reads as "the arm is 2,781.1 us short", and those are different campaign states. WHAT IS OBSERVED AND UNEXPLAINED: the optimizer holds roughly 16,400 us per step -- about 12.4 percent -- and in thirty-five cycles nothing has examined it as a ROUTE. It has been measured as a duration and never as a class with a floor. A not_closed line has named it three times and each time it was deferred because its bytes looked untouchable from the trace: _fused_adamw_ takes TensorLists, and the profiler records their Input Dims EMPTY, so every trace-join instrument in this sequence is structurally blind to it. So the class with the margin in it is the one class the instruments cannot see. WHY THAT IS AN OBSERVATION AND NOT A PLAN: the blindness is a property of the recorded trace that I can check, and the 2,781.1 us margin is a number already on a landed receipt. What is NOT yet stated is any mechanism -- whether the optimizer duration is bandwidth-bound at all, and whether the margin is available in it.

events.hypothesis: THE MECHANISM, named as a thing that is either true or false rather than as a restatement: the optimizer class is BANDWIDTH-BOUND OVER ITS OWN STATE FOOTPRINT, and its roughly 16,400 us per step is set by how many times that footprint crosses the memory bus, not by arithmetic and not by launch count. CONCRETELY. A fused AdamW step, per trainable parameter, READS the parameter, its gradient, its first moment and its second moment, and WRITES the parameter, both moments, and (wherever the gradient is cleared rather than reused) the gradient again. That is a fixed small number of traversals of a footprint whose size is decided by the trainable-parameter count and the dtype of each of those four tensors -- quantities the checkpoint and the optimizer-state inventory both record exactly. The arithmetic between the reads and the writes is a handful of FLOPs per element, so on this card the class cannot be compute-bound; if the mechanism is true, duration is footprint times traversals divided by achieved bandwidth, and nothing else. WHAT THE MECHANISM PREDICTS, WHICH IS WHY IT IS AN EXPLANATION AND NOT A LABEL. It predicts a FLOOR that is computable WITHOUT the trace: the necessary traffic is the footprint times the minimum traversal count a correct fused AdamW must perform. Measured duration ABOVE that floor is the removable part -- redundant traversals, an unfused path, state held in a wider dtype than the update needs, or gradient clearing as a separate pass. Measured duration AT the floor means the class is already at its bandwidth limit and supplies NONE of the 2,781.1 us the bar needs, which would close the optimizer as a route and leave the campaign needing a different third lever. WHY THIS SURVIVES THE INSTRUMENT BLINDNESS THAT DEFERRED IT THREE TIMES. The profiler records _fused_adamw_ Input Dims as EMPTY because it takes TensorLists, so every trace-join instrument in this campaign is structurally unable to size this class -- and that is exactly why it has been skipped. But the mechanism above does not need the trace: the footprint comes from the parameter and optimizer-state inventory, and the duration comes from the device timeline, which records the kernel regardless of whether its dims were captured. The two halves of the comparison come from two different sources, neither of which is the blind one.

events.refuted_if: REFUTED IF the optimizer class REMOVABLE time -- measured optimizer device time per step MINUS the bandwidth floor implied by its own state footprint -- is BELOW 2,781.1 us per step. THE THRESHOLD IS DERIVED FROM THE BAR AND NOT FROM THE DATA, and it is fixed here before any number is read: governed step 0.16376 s; 1.5x needs the step at 0.109173 s, a removal of 54,586.7 us; the two levers already priced supply all-device-idle 32,700.0 us and maximal elementwise fusion 19,105.6 us, capped composite 51,805.6; the shortfall is 54,586.7 - 51,805.6 = 2,781.1 us. That is exactly what a third lever must supply, so it is exactly the bar this class must clear to be the lever that decides the arm. THE FLOOR IS THE HONEST, MOST HOSTILE FORM OF THE COMPARISON. necessary_bytes = sum over the four AdamW tensors of trainable_elements x dtype_size, times the MINIMUM traversal count a correct fused AdamW must perform (read p, grad, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq; write p, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq), and floor_us = necessary_bytes / (1008 GB/s) x 1e6 -- 1008 being the PUBLISHED specification used to express a fraction, never a measured ceiling and never an impossibility premise. Using the published rate makes the floor as LOW as it can be and therefore the removable excess as LARGE as it can be, so the criterion is biased toward SUPPORTING the hypothesis; a refutation under it is a real refutation. SUPPORTED IF removable >= 2,781.1 us -- and the update must then say which sub-mechanism carries the excess (redundant traversals, an unfused path, state wider than the update needs, or a separate gradient-clearing pass), because "there is excess" names no treatment. INCONCLUSIVE IS RESERVED, and narrowly: only if the optimizer device kernels cannot be identified in the timeline at all, or the trainable-parameter footprint cannot be read from the inventory. A number that lands just under 2,781.1 is a REFUTATION, not an inconclusive result, and cycle 35 already proved the reverse case -- 19,105.6 against 21,886.7, ruled SUPPORTED at a 12.7 percent margin rather than softened. The same discipline binds in this direction.
events.instrument: ANALYSIS-ONLY, no card, no lease, no new capture -- and deliberately sourcing the two halves from two places, NEITHER of which is the blind one. DURATION: device timeline of cia-captured-trace-20260914T183257Z.json, the same 6 census windows and the same step-window clipping as cycles 33-35, filtered to optimizer kernels by symbol (fused adamw / multi_tensor / foreach) rather than by op name, since _fused_adamw_ Input Dims are EMPTY and that is precisely the blindness this design routes around. FOOTPRINT: the trainable-parameter count and the dtypes of parameter, gradient and both moments, read from the CIA hour custody checkpoint manifest and its optimizer-state identity block -- NOT from the trace. DELIBERATE RED FIRST, as every instrument in this sequence has done: run the filter against a trace window with no optimizer kernel present and require a non-zero exit with an explicit refusal rather than a zero, since a zero here would read as "the optimizer costs nothing" and support the refutation for the one reason that is not evidence.

events.because: The frozen criterion reads: "REFUTED IF the optimizer class REMOVABLE time -- measured optimizer device time per step MINUS the bandwidth floor implied by its own state footprint -- is BELOW 2,781.1 us per step." Removable is 10,234.0 us per step, so the criterion is not met and the hypothesis is SUPPORTED. THE ARITHMETIC, every width measured rather than assumed. Measured optimizer device time is 16,817.8 us/step over 46.7 kernels across three symbols (fused AdamW multi_tensor_apply 15,847.4; _ForeachUnaryOp behind _foreach_zero_ 963.9; _ForeachBinaryOpScalar 6.5). The state archive was walked as a zip with a stub unpickler: 702 bf16 moment storages, 948,060,160 elements, 1,896,120,320 bytes, exactly 2.0000 B/elem, plus 351 single-element fp32 step counters. 702 moment tensors is 351 parameters x 2 moments, giving 474,030,080 participating elements -- which the manifest independently corroborates at 474,029,824 changed elements, 0.0001 percent apart, from a field this instrument does not use in its arithmetic. The parameter width was measured as a RATIO, not assumed: core 502,858,033 bytes plus expert objects 5,662,593,375 over 3,082,539,008 declared elements is 2.0001 B/elem, resolving to bf16 within the 0.02 tolerance the script refuses outside of. The minimum correct fused AdamW traversal -- read param, grad, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq; write param and both moments -- is therefore 6,636,421,120 bytes, and at the PUBLISHED 1008 GB/s (a specification used to express a fraction, never a measured ceiling for this card and never an impossibility premise) the floor is 6,583.8 us/step. 16,817.8 - 6,583.8 = 10,234.0 us, which is 3.68x the 2,781.1 us the bar needs from a third lever. THE CRITERION WAS BIASED TOWARD THIS ANSWER AND THE RESULT SURVIVES REMOVING THE BIAS. The published rate makes the floor lowest and the excess largest, so support under it is the weakest form of support. Both hostile dtype variants were computed: gradient in fp32 raises the floor to 7,524.3 us (removable 9,293.5), and parameter and gradient both in fp32 raise it to 9,405.4 us (removable 7,412.4). Neither flips the verdict. The verdict flips only if this card sustains below 472.8 GB/s on this traffic -- 46.9 percent of the published rate -- which is a far larger correction than any dtype error could produce. THE INSTRUMENT REFUSES AN EMPTY CLASS, PROVED BEFORE THE GREEN RUN. --prove-red drops the optimizer symbols from the filter and the script exits 2 rather than publishing a zero, because zero removable time reads as "the optimizer costs nothing" (a finding) while an empty match means "this instrument did not find the optimizer" (a defect), and those are opposite in meaning and identical in arithmetic. With no counterpart seat to issue a PASS, that deliberate red and the execution of the real consumer are what this verdict rests on. WHAT THIS VERDICT IS NOT. Removable time is the distance between a measurement and a floor. It is not a ceiling on any treatment, not a claim that any mechanism collects it, and not an assertion about what this card can do. No arm is named by this ruling.

events.hypothesis: WHICH SUB-MECHANISM CARRIES THE EXCESS -- the criterion required this, and the honest answer is partial, so it is given as one measured term, one ELIMINATED candidate, and one open remainder. (1) MEASURED, 963.9 us: the separate gradient-clearing pass is real and is one of the four named candidates. _ForeachUnaryOp_cu sits behind aten::_foreach_zero_ x128 per step and costs 963.9 us/step, which is traffic no correct fused AdamW needs, since a fused step can consume the gradient in place. (2) ELIMINATED: "state wider than the update needs" is REFUTED by this cycle own split. The moments are already bf16 at exactly 2.0000 B/elem, and the parameters are bf16 too. There is no narrowing left to take; the dtype lever on this class is already spent, and any future proposal to narrow optimizer state is answered by this receipt. (3) OPEN, about 9,270 us: the fused kernel itself measures 15,847.4 us against a 6,583.8 us whole-class floor, roughly 2.4x the minimum traffic, and nothing in this cycle attributes that. Twenty-one device kernels per step carry 128 aten::_fused_adamw_ calls, so the class is decidedly NOT launch-bound at 754.6 us per kernel, which leaves redundant traversals or an unfused interior as the two surviving candidates and does not choose between them. WHAT THE REFUTATION DID NOT CLOSE, and what this SUPPORT does not open. A SUPPORTED verdict here closes nothing about routes either: it says the optimizer CONTAINS the 2,781.1 us shortfall with room to spare, not that any mechanism collects it. The three levers now priced (idle 32,700.0, elementwise 19,105.6, optimizer 10,234.0) act on different milliseconds only if they do not contend, and contention has NOT been checked -- the optimizer runs strictly after backward on one stream, which is precisely the serialization the idle lever claims, so these two may be pricing overlapping milliseconds and summing them would be the contending-ceilings error. That check is the successor and it outranks naming a treatment. NOT CLOSED, carried forward: no MEASURED device-memory traffic exists for these kernels, so the floor is an estimate of algorithmically necessary traffic, which the governed-run evidence contract requires to be reported separately from measured traffic; the gradient width is inferred from the parameter width rather than read from a receipt, though both hostile variants were run; the trace is a profiled run whose window span is instrumentation-dominated, so only per-step device figures are used and no wall-clock composition crosses that boundary; and the 128 aten::_fused_adamw_ calls against 1,195 param_groups is an unexamined shape that may itself be the redundant-traversal mechanism.

events.because: SUPPORTED at 10,234.0 us removable against a 2,781.1 us bar, 3.68x, robust across both hostile dtype variants and down to 46.9 percent of published bandwidth; the deliberate red proved the instrument refuses an empty class rather than publishing a zero. Successor opened on the contention question, which outranks naming a treatment because the optimizer runs strictly after backward on one stream and may be pricing the same milliseconds the idle lever already claims.

A not_closed line has named it three times and each time it was deferred because its bytes looked untouchable from the trace: _fused_adamw_ takes TensorLists, and the profiler records their Input Dims EMPTY, so every trace-join instrument in this sequence is structurally blind to it. hypotheses.explanation: THE MECHANISM, named as a thing that is either true or false rather than as a restatement: the optimizer class is BANDWIDTH-BOUND OVER ITS OWN STATE FOOTPRINT, and its roughly 16,400 us per step is set by how many times that footprint crosses the memory bus, not by arithmetic and not by launch count. CONCRETELY. A fused AdamW step, per trainable parameter, READS the parameter, its gradient, its first moment and its second moment, and WRITES the parameter, both moments, and (wherever the gradient is cleared rather than reused) the gradient again. That is a fixed small number of traversals of a footprint whose size is decided by the trainable-parameter count and the dtype of each of those four tensors -- quantities the checkpoint and the optimizer-state inventory both record exactly. The arithmetic between the reads and the writes is a handful of FLOPs per element, so on this card the class cannot be compute-bound; if the mechanism is true, duration is footprint times traversals divided by achieved bandwidth, and nothing else. WHAT THE MECHANISM PREDICTS, WHICH IS WHY IT IS AN EXPLANATION AND NOT A LABEL. It predicts a FLOOR that is computable WITHOUT the trace: the necessary traffic is the footprint times the minimum traversal count a correct fused AdamW must perform. Measured duration ABOVE that floor is the removable part -- redundant traversals, an unfused path, state held in a wider dtype than the update needs, or gradient clearing as a separate pass. Measured duration AT the floor means the class is already at its bandwidth limit and supplies NONE of the 2,781.1 us the bar needs, which would close the optimizer as a route and leave the campaign needing a different third lever. WHY THIS SURVIVES THE INSTRUMENT BLINDNESS THAT DEFERRED IT THREE TIMES. The profiler records _fused_adamw_ Input Dims as EMPTY because it takes TensorLists, so every trace-join instrument in this campaign is structurally unable to size this class -- and that is exactly why it has been skipped. But the mechanism above does not need the trace: the footprint comes from the parameter and optimizer-state inventory, and the duration comes from the device timeline, which records the kernel regardless of whether its dims were captured. The two halves of the comparison come from two different sources, neither of which is the blind one.
hypotheses.criterion: REFUTED IF the optimizer class REMOVABLE time -- measured optimizer device time per step MINUS the bandwidth floor implied by its own state footprint -- is BELOW 2,781.1 us per step. THE THRESHOLD IS DERIVED FROM THE BAR AND NOT FROM THE DATA, and it is fixed here before any number is read: governed step 0.16376 s; 1.5x needs the step at 0.109173 s, a removal of 54,586.7 us; the two levers already priced supply all-device-idle 32,700.0 us and maximal elementwise fusion 19,105.6 us, capped composite 51,805.6; the shortfall is 54,586.7 - 51,805.6 = 2,781.1 us. That is exactly what a third lever must supply, so it is exactly the bar this class must clear to be the lever that decides the arm. THE FLOOR IS THE HONEST, MOST HOSTILE FORM OF THE COMPARISON. necessary_bytes = sum over the four AdamW tensors of trainable_elements x dtype_size, times the MINIMUM traversal count a correct fused AdamW must perform (read p, grad, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq; write p, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq), and floor_us = necessary_bytes / (1008 GB/s) x 1e6 -- 1008 being the PUBLISHED specification used to express a fraction, never a measured ceiling and never an impossibility premise. Using the published rate makes the floor as LOW as it can be and therefore the removable excess as LARGE as it can be, so the criterion is biased toward SUPPORTING the hypothesis; a refutation under it is a real refutation. DURATION: device timeline of cia-captured-trace-20260914T183257Z.json, the same 6 census windows and the same step-window clipping as cycles 33-35, filtered to optimizer kernels by symbol (fused adamw / multi_tensor / foreach) rather than by op name, since _fused_adamw_ Input Dims are EMPTY and that is precisely the blindness this design routes around. FOOTPRINT: the trainable-parameter count and the dtypes of parameter, gradient and both moments, read from the CIA hour custody checkpoint manifest and its optimizer-state identity block -- NOT from the trace. DELIBERATE RED FIRST, as every instrument in this sequence has done: run the filter against a trace window with no optimizer kernel present and require a non-zero exit with an explicit refusal rather than a zero, since a zero here would read as "the optimizer costs nothing" and support the refutation for the one reason that is not evidence.
hypotheses.ruling: The frozen criterion reads: "REFUTED IF the optimizer class REMOVABLE time -- measured optimizer device time per step MINUS the bandwidth floor implied by its own state footprint -- is BELOW 2,781.1 us per step." Removable is 10,234.0 us per step, so the criterion is not met and the hypothesis is SUPPORTED. THE ARITHMETIC, every width measured rather than assumed. Measured optimizer device time is 16,817.8 us/step over 46.7 kernels across three symbols (fused AdamW multi_tensor_apply 15,847.4; _ForeachUnaryOp behind _foreach_zero_ 963.9; _ForeachBinaryOpScalar 6.5). The state archive was walked as a zip with a stub unpickler: 702 bf16 moment storages, 948,060,160 elements, 1,896,120,320 bytes, exactly 2.0000 B/elem, plus 351 single-element fp32 step counters. 702 moment tensors is 351 parameters x 2 moments, giving 474,030,080 participating elements -- which the manifest independently corroborates at 474,029,824 changed elements, 0.0001 percent apart, from a field this instrument does not use in its arithmetic. The parameter width was measured as a RATIO, not assumed: core 502,858,033 bytes plus expert objects 5,662,593,375 over 3,082,539,008 declared elements is 2.0001 B/elem, resolving to bf16 within the 0.02 tolerance the script refuses outside of. The minimum correct fused AdamW traversal -- read param, grad, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq; write param and both moments -- is therefore 6,636,421,120 bytes, and at the PUBLISHED 1008 GB/s (a specification used to express a fraction, never a measured ceiling for this card and never an impossibility premise) the floor is 6,583.8 us/step. 16,817.8 - 6,583.8 = 10,234.0 us, which is 3.68x the 2,781.1 us the bar needs from a third lever. THE CRITERION WAS BIASED TOWARD THIS ANSWER AND THE RESULT SURVIVES REMOVING THE BIAS. The published rate makes the floor lowest and the excess largest, so support under it is the weakest form of support. Both hostile dtype variants were computed: gradient in fp32 raises the floor to 7,524.3 us (removable 9,293.5), and parameter and gradient both in fp32 raise it to 9,405.4 us (removable 7,412.4). Neither flips the verdict. The verdict flips only if this card sustains below 472.8 GB/s on this traffic -- 46.9 percent of the published rate -- which is a far larger correction than any dtype error could produce. THE INSTRUMENT REFUSES AN EMPTY CLASS, PROVED BEFORE THE GREEN RUN. --prove-red drops the optimizer symbols from the filter and the script exits 2 rather than publishing a zero, because zero removable time reads as "the optimizer costs nothing" (a finding) while an empty match means "this instrument did not find the optimizer" (a defect), and those are opposite in meaning and identical in arithmetic. With no counterpart seat to issue a PASS, that deliberate red and the execution of the real consumer are what this verdict rests on. WHAT THIS VERDICT IS NOT. Removable time is the distance between a measurement and a floor. It is not a ceiling on any treatment, not a claim that any mechanism collects it, and not an assertion about what this card can do. No arm is named by this ruling.
hypotheses.not_closed: WHICH SUB-MECHANISM CARRIES THE EXCESS -- the criterion required this, and the honest answer is partial, so it is given as one measured term, one ELIMINATED candidate, and one open remainder. (1) MEASURED, 963.9 us: the separate gradient-clearing pass is real and is one of the four named candidates. _ForeachUnaryOp_cu sits behind aten::_foreach_zero_ x128 per step and costs 963.9 us/step, which is traffic no correct fused AdamW needs, since a fused step can consume the gradient in place. (2) ELIMINATED: "state wider than the update needs" is REFUTED by this cycle own split. The moments are already bf16 at exactly 2.0000 B/elem, and the parameters are bf16 too. There is no narrowing left to take; the dtype lever on this class is already spent, and any future proposal to narrow optimizer state is answered by this receipt. (3) OPEN, about 9,270 us: the fused kernel itself measures 15,847.4 us against a 6,583.8 us whole-class floor, roughly 2.4x the minimum traffic, and nothing in this cycle attributes that. Twenty-one device kernels per step carry 128 aten::_fused_adamw_ calls, so the class is decidedly NOT launch-bound at 754.6 us per kernel, which leaves redundant traversals or an unfused interior as the two surviving candidates and does not choose between them. A SUPPORTED verdict here closes nothing about routes either: it says the optimizer CONTAINS the 2,781.1 us shortfall with room to spare, not that any mechanism collects it. The three levers now priced (idle 32,700.0, elementwise 19,105.6, optimizer 10,234.0) act on different milliseconds only if they do not contend, and contention has NOT been checked -- the optimizer runs strictly after backward on one stream, which is precisely the serialization the idle lever claims, so these two may be pricing overlapping milliseconds and summing them would be the contending-ceilings error. That check is the successor and it outranks naming a treatment. NOT CLOSED, carried forward: no MEASURED device-memory traffic exists for these kernels, so the floor is an estimate of algorithmically necessary traffic, which the governed-run evidence contract requires to be reported separately from measured traffic; the gradient width is inferred from the parameter width rather than read from a receipt, though both hostile variants were run; the trace is a profiled run whose window span is instrumentation-dominated, so only per-step device figures are used and no wall-clock composition crosses that boundary; and the 128 aten::_fused_adamw_ calls against 1,195 param_groups is an unexamined shape that may itself be the redundant-traversal mechanism.
hypotheses.closing: SUPPORTED at 10,234.0 us removable against a 2,781.1 us bar, 3.68x, robust across both hostile dtype variants and down to 46.9 percent of published bandwidth; the deliberate red proved the instrument refuses an empty class rather than publishing a zero. Successor opened on the contention question, which outranks naming a treatment because the optimizer runs strictly after backward on one stream and may be pricing the same milliseconds the idle lever already claims.

The registry query on this proposition returned a row that answers HALF of it and was never applied to these levers: device-timeline-has-zero-concurrency-single-stream-20260914 measured all 44,632 kernels on stream 7 with the sum of durations EQUAL to the interval union, so no two kernels overlap in TIME. events.hypothesis: THE MECHANISM, stated so it is either true or false. The three levers are DISJOINT POPULATIONS of device microseconds, so their removals compose additively up to the limit of what each class contains. Concretely: idle is the complement of the busy interval union inside the census windows, so by construction it shares no microsecond with any kernel; and the elementwise and optimizer kernel sets are disjoint because the two selectors match different kernel families, so no kernel microsecond is claimed by both levers. If that is true, the 62,039.6 us stack is a real composition over distinct time and the bar is reachable by these three levers together. If it is false -- if the selectors share kernels -- then the shared microseconds are counted twice, the honest composite is the union rather than the sum, and the stack shrinks by the shared amount. WHY THIS IS AN EXPLANATION AND NOT A LABEL: it predicts a measurable quantity, the intersection of two symbol-selected kernel sets over the same census windows, and the prediction is falsifiable in one pass over a trace already on disk. It also predicts the SIGN of any error -- a positive intersection can only SHRINK the stack, never grow it -- so the check can only move the campaign toward a more hostile number, which is the direction a check should be able to go. WHAT IT DOES NOT EXPLAIN, named now rather than discovered later: disjoint POPULATIONS do not make the three removals independent ACTIONS. A shorter kernel sequence can change how much device idle exists, and a fused elementwise path changes which kernels the optimizer waits behind. That is mechanism interaction, it is a different question from double counting, and this cycle does not touch it.

If that launch had not returned by a, the device was waiting on the host: HOST_DISPATCH, and consistent with launch-bound execution. If the launch had already returned before a, the host was done and the device waited on something else: DEPENDENCY. A hole whose closer resolves to no launch call is UNATTRIBUTED and is never folded into either class. WHY THE HEADLINE IS A COUNT AND NOT A DURATION, which is the same principle cycles 38-41 established and which points the other way here. The trace spans ~503,890 us per window against a 163,760 us governed step, so absolute hole DURATIONS are instrumentation-dominated and the governed-run evidence contract separation clause forbids composing them with a governed figure. Hole COUNT survives profiling, because stretching an interval neither creates nor destroys a launch boundary. The prior receipt puts DEPENDENCY at 2.3% of profiled idle DURATION and about 36% of hole COUNT, and those disagree by more than an order of magnitude precisely because the profiler inflates host-side time. The duration figure is the one the profiler corrupts. THE BIAS DIRECTION IS NAMED BEFORE THE RUN AND IT RUNS AGAINST THE REFUTATION. Profiling LENGTHENS every launch call, so a launch that truly returned before a hole began can appear still-open under the profiler. That misclassifies DEPENDENCY holes as HOST_DISPATCH and never the reverse, so the measured dependency count share is a LOWER BOUND on the true one and any refutation computed from it is conservative. TWO POPULATIONS, AND THE VERDICT BINDS ON THE ONE MOST FAVOURABLE TO THE COMPOSITION. The prior split ran over all device categories (~7,906.7 holes per step); cycles 38-41 priced gaps over kernels only (7,437.7). Both are computed and the verdict uses the SMALLER dependency share, so the composition is refuted only if it fails on its better reading. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM. A DEPENDENCY hole is not unreachable idle in general -- a whole-step graph with the optimizer on a second stream targets exactly that population, and it is a DIFFERENT lever from the launch-rate one the 32,700.0 us figure prices. This measures what the IDLE LEVER AS PRICED cannot reach, and scaling it is not the same as retiring the route.

events.observation: Cycle 42 audited the IDLE lever's maximal-effectiveness premise and found 36.4% of its target population unreachable by the mechanism that priced it, which refuted the three-lever 1.5x composition. The other two levers have had no such audit. This cycle audits the ELEMENTWISE lever, 19,105.6 us per step, whose own instrument states the premise in its docstring: "every intermediate held in registers, every pure copy absorbed ... It does not prove any two kernels are actually adjacent in a dataflow sense." FIRST, A QUESTION FROM THE CYCLE-42 LEDGER IS ANSWERED BY READING THE SOURCE RATHER THAN BY MEASURING, AND THE ANSWER IS NO. I wrote that the elementwise figure might already contain launch or idle time the idle lever ALSO counts. It does not: the per-kernel credit is min(dur_us, excess + eliminable_byte_time) summed over kernel DEVICE durations, so the whole 19,105.6 us is bounded by and composed of device time inside elementwise kernels. No host time and no inter-kernel hole enters it. The real overlap with the idle lever is the one cycle 41 already measured -- the gaps adjacent to retired kernels, 0.18899 of the idle lever -- and that is a different quantity, already netted out. SECOND, A FIGURE I PUBLISHED IN THAT SAME LEDGER BLOCK IS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE. I wrote that the lever implies 16.3 us per removed kernel against 1,172.3 kernels, "far above a typical elementwise kernel's device time". That divides the WHOLE lever by only the fully-removed count. The receipt's own split is 1,172.3 kernels removed outright for 8,634.1 us, which is 7.365 us each and entirely ordinary; the remaining 10,471.5 us is partial credit spread across the other ~2,274.7 kernels of the 3,447.0-kernel class. There was no anomaly there.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM. The byte half of the lever credits each kernel with shedding ONE traversal of its largest tensor -- the single crossing of the intermediate it produces or consumes. That traversal is elidable only if the kernel on the OTHER SIDE of that edge sits inside the same fused group. So take each elementwise kernel's immediate device PREDECESSOR and SUCCESSOR over the full in-window kernel timeline. If neither is in the elementwise class, the kernel has no in-class neighbour on either edge, no fusion within this class can hold its intermediate in a register, and the value is materialized across a class boundary: ISOLATED. At least one in-class neighbour: GROUPED, a candidate fusible edge exists. ADJACENCY IS A PROXY FOR DATAFLOW AND ITS BIAS IS NAMED BEFORE THE RUN. Two adjacent elementwise kernels need not be dataflow-connected, so adjacency OVER-counts fusibility. GROUPED is an upper bound on the genuinely fusible set and ISOLATED is a LOWER bound on the unreachable one, so every figure is conservative in the direction that spares the lever and any refutation computed from it is safe to act on. This is the same bias structure cycle 42 carried, pointing the same way. WHAT IS CHARGED, AND IT IS THE SMALLER OF TWO DEFENSIBLE ACCOUNTINGS. Only the eliminable-byte part of an isolated kernel's credit is an INTERMEDIATE claim; the excess part is device time above a published-rate byte ideal and says nothing about registers. So an isolated kernel keeps min(dur, excess) and is charged only the remainder. Charging the whole composite would have produced the larger number. THE BYTE MODEL IS INHERITED, THE DISCRIMINATOR IS AUTHORED. Byte counting, the elementwise selector, the 1008 GB/s reference and the per-kernel cap are imported from elementwise_byte_reduction_ceiling so the two receipts describe the same lever to the last microsecond; the adjacency classification is the thing under test and is written from the trace. WHY THIS IS A COUNT-ADJACENT MEASURE AND NOT A DURATION COMPOSITION. Class membership of a neighbour is a property of the kernel sequence, which profiling does not change -- stretching an interval neither creates nor destroys a kernel. The charged microseconds are DEVICE durations from within the profiled trace, the same population the 19,105.6 us figure itself is built from, so this is a re-partition of an existing quantity rather than a new composition across the governed/profiled boundary.

events.refuted_if: REFUTED IF the unreachable charge on the ISOLATED set EXCEEDS 7,452.9 us per step. THE THRESHOLD IS FROZEN FROM THE BAR AND IS NOT CHOSEN HERE: 1.5x on the 0.16376 s governed step needs 54,586.7 us removed, the naive three-lever sum supplied 62,039.6 us, so the margin the composition ever had is exactly 7,452.9 us -- the same figure cycles 38, 39, 40 and 41 used unchanged. A lever whose unreachable part alone exceeds the entire margin the composition ever held is not a ceiling that was slightly optimistic; it is a ceiling of the same kind cycle 42 found overstated by 36%. ALSO REFUSED, independently of any share, IF THE CLASSIFICATION DEGENERATES: the instrument exits non-zero when the ISOLATED set is EMPTY, because an unreachable charge of 0.0 would read as "every credited microsecond is fusible" -- a FINDING that leaves the lever at its full 19,105.6 us -- while being equally consistent with a neighbour lookup that never resolves, which is a DEFECT; and when EVERY elementwise kernel is isolated, which with this class holding roughly half of all kernels is a broken timeline join rather than a fact about fusion. A sized coverage below 0.50 also refuses, because a thin sized population makes every isolated kernel charge nothing and the lever would pass for the one reason that is not evidence. I DO NOT PREDICT THE DIRECTION OF THIS ONE, and I am saying so before the run because I predicted cycle 42's refutation in writing and that is only creditable if I also say when I cannot. The elementwise class holds roughly half the kernels in the step, which argues that most of them have an in-class neighbour and the lever largely survives; against that, the class's largest credited sites are aten::copy_ and aten::add_ on residual-stream shapes, which sit between GEMMs by construction. Those two considerations point opposite ways and I have not measured which dominates.
events.supported_if: SUPPORTED IF the unreachable charge is at or below 7,452.9 us per step: the lever's maximal-fusion premise survives an adjacency audit at the scale that matters to the composition, and the elementwise figure stands as priced apart from a correction smaller than the margin. Note that SUPPORTED here does NOT revive the 1.5x composition -- cycle 42 ruled it REFUTED at 46,199.7 us against 54,586.7 needed, and this cycle can only lower that. A SUPPORTED verdict means the remaining shortfall is not attributable to this lever. INCONCLUSIVE only if the run does not discriminate -- for instance if the isolated set is non-empty but carries so little credited time that the partition says nothing about the premise either way. Never for a number that is merely unwelcome.

hypotheses.observation: Cycle 42 audited the IDLE lever's maximal-effectiveness premise and found 36.4% of its target population unreachable by the mechanism that priced it, which refuted the three-lever 1.5x composition. The other two levers have had no such audit. This cycle audits the ELEMENTWISE lever, 19,105.6 us per step, whose own instrument states the premise in its docstring: "every intermediate held in registers, every pure copy absorbed ... It does not prove any two kernels are actually adjacent in a dataflow sense." FIRST, A QUESTION FROM THE CYCLE-42 LEDGER IS ANSWERED BY READING THE SOURCE RATHER THAN BY MEASURING, AND THE ANSWER IS NO. I wrote that the elementwise figure might already contain launch or idle time the idle lever ALSO counts. It does not: the per-kernel credit is min(dur_us, excess + eliminable_byte_time) summed over kernel DEVICE durations, so the whole 19,105.6 us is bounded by and composed of device time inside elementwise kernels. No host time and no inter-kernel hole enters it. The real overlap with the idle lever is the one cycle 41 already measured -- the gaps adjacent to retired kernels, 0.18899 of the idle lever -- and that is a different quantity, already netted out. SECOND, A FIGURE I PUBLISHED IN THAT SAME LEDGER BLOCK IS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE. I wrote that the lever implies 16.3 us per removed kernel against 1,172.3 kernels, "far above a typical elementwise kernel's device time". That divides the WHOLE lever by only the fully-removed count. The receipt's own split is 1,172.3 kernels removed outright for 8,634.1 us, which is 7.365 us each and entirely ordinary; the remaining 10,471.5 us is partial credit spread across the other ~2,274.7 kernels of the 3,447.0-kernel class. There was no anomaly there.
hypotheses.explanation: MECHANISM. The byte half of the lever credits each kernel with shedding ONE traversal of its largest tensor -- the single crossing of the intermediate it produces or consumes. That traversal is elidable only if the kernel on the OTHER SIDE of that edge sits inside the same fused group. So take each elementwise kernel's immediate device PREDECESSOR and SUCCESSOR over the full in-window kernel timeline. If neither is in the elementwise class, the kernel has no in-class neighbour on either edge, no fusion within this class can hold its intermediate in a register, and the value is materialized across a class boundary: ISOLATED. At least one in-class neighbour: GROUPED, a candidate fusible edge exists. ADJACENCY IS A PROXY FOR DATAFLOW AND ITS BIAS IS NAMED BEFORE THE RUN. Two adjacent elementwise kernels need not be dataflow-connected, so adjacency OVER-counts fusibility. GROUPED is an upper bound on the genuinely fusible set and ISOLATED is a LOWER bound on the unreachable one, so every figure is conservative in the direction that spares the lever and any refutation computed from it is safe to act on. This is the same bias structure cycle 42 carried, pointing the same way. WHAT IS CHARGED, AND IT IS THE SMALLER OF TWO DEFENSIBLE ACCOUNTINGS. Only the eliminable-byte part of an isolated kernel's credit is an INTERMEDIATE claim; the excess part is device time above a published-rate byte ideal and says nothing about registers. So an isolated kernel keeps min(dur, excess) and is charged only the remainder. Charging the whole composite would have produced the larger number. THE BYTE MODEL IS INHERITED, THE DISCRIMINATOR IS AUTHORED. Byte counting, the elementwise selector, the 1008 GB/s reference and the per-kernel cap are imported from elementwise_byte_reduction_ceiling so the two receipts describe the same lever to the last microsecond; the adjacency classification is the thing under test and is written from the trace. WHY THIS IS A COUNT-ADJACENT MEASURE AND NOT A DURATION COMPOSITION. Class membership of a neighbour is a property of the kernel sequence, which profiling does not change -- stretching an interval neither creates nor destroys a kernel. The charged microseconds are DEVICE durations from within the profiled trace, the same population the 19,105.6 us figure itself is built from, so this is a re-partition of an existing quantity rather than a new composition across the governed/profiled boundary.
hypotheses.criterion: REFUTED IF the unreachable charge on the ISOLATED set EXCEEDS 7,452.9 us per step. THE THRESHOLD IS FROZEN FROM THE BAR AND IS NOT CHOSEN HERE: 1.5x on the 0.16376 s governed step needs 54,586.7 us removed, the naive three-lever sum supplied 62,039.6 us, so the margin the composition ever had is exactly 7,452.9 us -- the same figure cycles 38, 39, 40 and 41 used unchanged. A lever whose unreachable part alone exceeds the entire margin the composition ever held is not a ceiling that was slightly optimistic; it is a ceiling of the same kind cycle 42 found overstated by 36%. ALSO REFUSED, independently of any share, IF THE CLASSIFICATION DEGENERATES: the instrument exits non-zero when the ISOLATED set is EMPTY, because an unreachable charge of 0.0 would read as "every credited microsecond is fusible" -- a FINDING that leaves the lever at its full 19,105.6 us -- while being equally consistent with a neighbour lookup that never resolves, which is a DEFECT; and when EVERY elementwise kernel is isolated, which with this class holding roughly half of all kernels is a broken timeline join rather than a fact about fusion. A sized coverage below 0.50 also refuses, because a thin sized population makes every isolated kernel charge nothing and the lever would pass for the one reason that is not evidence. I DO NOT PREDICT THE DIRECTION OF THIS ONE, and I am saying so before the run because I predicted cycle 42's refutation in writing and that is only creditable if I also say when I cannot. The elementwise class holds roughly half the kernels in the step, which argues that most of them have an in-class neighbour and the lever largely survives; against that, the class's largest credited sites are aten::copy_ and aten::add_ on residual-stream shapes, which sit between GEMMs by construction. Those two considerations point opposite ways and I have not measured which dominates.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM. This card has 72 MB of L2 and the standing explanation for three device classes reporting ABOVE the published DRAM rate -- elementwise 1.151, reduce 1.633, triton_fused 2.253 -- is a working set around 25 MB sitting inside it. So the sign of a kernel's residual against a DRAM-rate ideal is expected to track its working set. A kernel whose sized bytes fit in L2 can beat the DRAM rate, and a positive residual there is NOT explained by traffic, so it is admissible as overhead a treatment might collect. A kernel whose sized bytes EXCEED L2 must go to DRAM for the remainder, so its shortfall against the same ideal is TRAFFIC -- and traffic is already priced by the byte half of this very lever. Charging it again to the excess half is the same microseconds counted twice, inside one lever, which is exactly the defect the per-kernel cap was written to prevent between the halves and does not prevent within one of them. THREE READINGS OF THE ESTIMATOR ARE PUBLISHED so it is checkable rather than asserted: the one-sided sum at the published rate, which must reproduce 7,017.0 us or the instrument is describing a different lever; the TWO-sided sum at the same rate, which is the quantity any class-level statement about overhead actually rests on; and the one-sided sum recomputed with the reference set to the class's own measured achieved rate, so the class no longer beats its own reference. THE WORKING-SET TEST IS A PROXY AND ITS LIMIT IS NAMED BEFORE THE RUN. No L2 hit-rate counter exists in this build, so this is a working-set test and not a residency measurement: a kernel under 72 MB can still miss L2 because it shares the cache with everything else in flight, and a kernel above it can hit on part of its traffic. The first error makes the L2_RESIDENT set too large and therefore the DRAM_BOUND charge too small, which spares the lever; the second makes the charge too large. The two do not cancel and I cannot sign the net, so unlike cycles 42 and 43 this instrument does NOT carry a one-directional bias argument, and that is stated rather than manufactured.

events.refuted_if: REFUTED IF the one-sided excess sitting on DRAM_BOUND kernels -- those whose sized working set exceeds the 72 MB L2 capacity -- EXCEEDS 4,730.5 us per step. THE THRESHOLD IS A ROUTE-SELECTION THRESHOLD AND IS STATED AS SUCH RATHER THAN DRESSED AS THE BAR. The 1.5x question is already settled: cycle 42 ruled the three-lever composition REFUTED at 46,199.7 us against 54,586.7 needed and cycle 43 lowered it to 42,058.6 us. No further reduction of any lever can change that verdict, so a threshold derived from 1.5x could only be a criterion that cannot fail, which the loop forbids. The live question is which lever the campaign should pursue next, and the threshold that changes that answer is the one that REORDERS the two audited levers: the elementwise lever stands at 14,964.5 us after cycle 43 and the optimizer lever at 10,234.0 us, so a double-counted charge above their difference of 4,730.5 us drops elementwise below optimizer and inverts the campaign's own ranking. ALSO REFUSED, independently of any charge, IF THE PARTITION DEGENERATES: the instrument exits non-zero when the DRAM_BOUND set is EMPTY, because an excess that is 100% admissible overhead would read as "the estimator is sound" -- a FINDING that leaves the excess half fully spendable -- while being equally consistent with a size join that resolved nothing, a DEFECT; and when EVERY kernel is DRAM_BOUND, which contradicts the class achieving above the published rate and is a broken join rather than a finding. Sized coverage below 0.50 also refuses, and that is the branch proved red before this cycle opened. I DO NOT PREDICT THE DIRECTION. The class's largest sites include aten::copy_ and aten::fill_ at [4096, 32768], which is 256 MiB at bf16 and far above L2, and those carry real device time; against that, most of the 3,447.0 kernels per step are small residual-stream and expert shapes well inside 72 MB. Which population holds the positive residual is what the run decides.
events.supported_if: SUPPORTED IF the DRAM_BOUND excess is at or below 4,730.5 us per step: the one-sided clamp is not concealing a material double count of traffic the byte half already prices, the elementwise lever remains the larger of the two audited levers, and the campaign's ranking of routes stands. SUPPORTED does NOT mean the excess half is overhead a treatment collects -- it means the part of it attributable to DRAM traffic is too small to reorder the routes. Whether the remaining L2-resident excess is collectible at all is a separate and untouched question. INCONCLUSIVE only if the run does not discriminate -- for instance if the two-sided reading and the working-set partition disagree about which population carries the residual, which would mean the reference rate rather than the cache is doing the work. Never for a number that is merely unwelcome.

events.hypothesis: THE FINDING THIS CYCLE PRODUCED OUTSIDE ITS OWN CRITERION, AND IT IS LARGER THAN THE ONE IT RULED. The 1.5x question is already settled: cycle 42 ruled the three-lever composition REFUTED at 46,199.7 us against 54,586.7 needed and cycle 43 lowered it to 42,058.6 us. They hold 3,469.8 us of device time -- 12.6% of the class -- and carry just 151.2 us of the one-sided excess, because they are the large aten::copy_ and aten::fill_ sites that already run near or above the published rate. events.hypothesis: MECHANISM. A single class-wide reference rate treats every elementwise kernel as having the same achievable bandwidth, and they do not. A [2048, 1024] add and a [4096, 32768] copy differ in access pattern, cache behaviour and achievable rate, and neither figure is a property a fusion changes except by changing the shape. So a residual measured against ONE class rate mixes two quantities. BETWEEN-SITE: this shape is slower than the class average -- a property of the shape, not overhead, collectible only by changing the shape. WITHIN-SITE: this INVOCATION is slower than other invocations of the SAME op on the SAME dims -- same work, same shape, different duration, and that is where per-kernel overhead would have to live if it lives anywhere. THE DISCRIMINATOR. Group kernels by SITE = (cpu_op name, recorded input dims), so every kernel in a site does the same work on the same shapes. Give each site its OWN mean duration as its reference and recompute the one-sided residual. A site's mean residual against its own mean is zero by construction, so what survives is exactly the positive half of WITHIN-SITE dispersion, with every shape-explained difference removed. The remainder of the priced 7,017.0 us is then the between-site part by subtraction. THE BIAS DIRECTION IS NAMED BEFORE THE RUN AND IT SPARES THE HYPOTHESIS THAT OVERHEAD EXISTS. Sites are formed from recorded input dims, so two genuinely different workloads sharing a dims string are merged into one site, which INFLATES within-site dispersion. Any finding that within-site dispersion is small is therefore conservative in the direction that would have preserved the lever. Single-invocation sites have zero within-site dispersion by construction and are excluded from the within-site figure and reported separately rather than scored as zero. WHAT A RESULT WOULD AND WOULD NOT LICENSE. A small within-site residual means the excess half is shape heterogeneity, and a fusion collects shape heterogeneity only by changing shapes -- which is the BYTE half of this same lever, already priced separately, so crediting it twice would be the double count the per-kernel cap was written to prevent. A large one does NOT establish that the dispersion is removable: scheduling, clock state, cache occupancy from neighbouring work and measurement noise all produce within-site dispersion. It bounds where overhead could be, never that it is there, and the artifact says so.

THE THRESHOLD IS A ROUTE-SELECTION THRESHOLD AND IS STATED AS SUCH, on the same basis cycle 44 used and updated for the new lever value. The 1.5x question is settled: cycles 42 and 43 ruled the three-lever composition REFUTED and no further reduction of any lever can change that, so a threshold derived from 1.5x would be a criterion that cannot fail, which the loop forbids. The live question is which lever to pursue next, and the threshold that changes that answer reorders the two audited levers: elementwise stands at 14,813.3 us after cycle 44 and the optimizer at 10,234.0 us, so 4,579.3 us is the difference. ALSO REFUSED, independently of any residual, IF THE SITE GROUPING DEGENERATES: the instrument exits non-zero when less than 50% of class device time sits in sites with more than one invocation, because within-site dispersion is 0.0 by construction for a single-invocation site and a near-zero residual would read as "the excess is entirely shape heterogeneity" -- a FINDING that retires 7,017.0 us of the lever -- while being equally consistent with a site key that grouped nothing, a DEFECT. That is the branch proved red before this cycle opened, by keying each kernel on its own start timestamp. Sized coverage below 0.50 also refuses. I PREDICT SUPPORTED, and I am saying so before the run. The class's device time is dominated by a small number of repeated residual-stream and expert shapes invoked tens of times per step, and cycle 44 already showed the two-sided residual is within 110 us of zero against the class's own rate, which is what between-site heterogeneity plus a near-symmetric within-site spread would look like. If that is right the excess half is not overhead and the elementwise lever is materially smaller than 14,813.3 us -- a prediction that costs me, which is why it is registered rather than left unstated.
