events.hypothesis: WHAT THIS RETIRES, AND IT IS THE LARGEST SINGLE RETIREMENT OF THE AUDIT. A fusion collects between-site heterogeneity only by changing the shapes, and changing the shapes is exactly what the BYTE half of this same lever prices -- 13,703.8 us of eliminable intermediate traversals. Crediting the between-site excess as well charges the same mechanism twice, which is the double count the per-kernel cap in the original instrument was written to prevent and did not catch, because the cap bounds a kernel against its own duration and cannot see that its two halves name one act. So 5,697.9 us/step comes off: elementwise lever 14,813.3 -> 9,115.4 us/step; three-lever stack 41,907.4 -> 36,209.5 of the 54,586.7 required, short by 18,377.2, about 1.28x. THE RANKING FLIPS, WHICH IS WHAT THE THRESHOLD WAS FOR. The elementwise lever now stands BELOW the optimizer lever (9,115.4 against 10,234.0) for the first time in this campaign. Three cycles ago it was 19,105.6 and was the largest of the three. A DEFECT IN MY OWN FROZEN CRITERION, RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY PASSED. I froze the threshold against the SURVIVING within-site residual and labelled it "the threshold that reorders the two levers". The quantity that actually reorders them is the RETIRED amount, so the exact flip condition is within-site < 2,437.7 us/step, not <= 4,579.3. The two are not the same number and I wrote them as though they were. The measured 1,319.1 clears BOTH readings, so the verdict and the reordering both stand on the arithmetic rather than on the looser wording -- but a criterion whose stated meaning and stated number disagree is a defect even when the result is insensitive to it, and it would not have been insensitive at 3,000 us. WHAT SURVIVES AND IS NOT CLOSED. The 1,319.1 us/step of within-site dispersion is NOT established as removable overhead and this cycle does not claim it is. Scheduling, clock and power state, L2 occupancy from neighbouring work, and measurement noise all produce within-site dispersion, and no counter in this build separates them from per-kernel launch cost. The number bounds where overhead COULD live -- 1,319.1 us/step, 4.8% of the class device time -- and nothing more. Also untouched: sites are keyed on recorded input dims, so two genuinely different workloads sharing a dims string merge into one site and inflate the within-site figure, which means the true within-site dispersion is at or below 1,319.1 and the retirement is if anything understated. THE SUCCESSOR IS THE OPTIMIZER LEVER AND IT INHERITS THIS EXACT QUESTION. 10,234.0 us is the last of the three with no audit at all, and it is distance to a bandwidth floor computed under the same published 1008.0 GB/s reference that this class exceeds by 6.5%. A floor computed under a rate the hardware beats is not a floor, and after this cycle it is also the LARGEST remaining lever.

events.hypothesis: TWO EXPLANATIONS, WITH OPPOSITE CONSEQUENCES FOR EVERY LEVER THIS CAMPAIGN HAS PUBLISHED. OVER-COUNT: the byte model credited the kernel with more bytes than it moved, in which case every byte figure downstream is inflated -- including the 13,703.8 us eliminable-bytes half of the elementwise lever, which is the single largest quantity in the entire audit and larger than any lever now standing. CACHE SERVICE: the bytes are real but part of the traffic never reached DRAM, in which case the byte COUNT is right and what is wrong is pricing those bytes at a DRAM rate, because some of them cost cache time instead of memory time. Both are defects; they are different defects and they are repaired differently. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS A PHYSICAL PER-KERNEL BOUND, NOT A CORRELATION. At most the whole L2 can be serving one kernel, so its DRAM traffic is at least (bytes - 72 MiB) and its apparent rate can exceed peak by at most peak * bytes / (bytes - 72 MiB). A kernel that exceeds even that cannot be explained by cache at all and its byte count must be wrong. WHY THE BOUND DISCRIMINATES RATHER THAN MERELY BOUNDING. It is a function of SIZE. A 100 MiB tensor can be 72% resident and inflate enormously; a 1 GiB tensor can be at most 7% resident and inflate by 7.6%. So the same measured inflation is innocent at one size and impossible at another, and each kernel is judged against its own size rather than the class against one number. If the defect were a fixed multiplicative error in the byte formula it would show up as inflation that does not care about size, which is exactly what this bound catches. THE BIAS IS NAMED BEFORE THE RUN AND IT SPARES THE BYTE MODEL. The ceiling assumes the entire cache is dedicated to this one kernel and hits on every byte it holds, which nothing else in flight would permit. That is maximally generous to the cache reading, so the bound is built to make refutation easy. SUPPORTED here -- the byte model over-counts -- is therefore the STRONG direction, and REFUTED is the weak one. Same bias structure as cycles 42 and 43, pointing the same way.

events.refuted_if: REFUTED IF at most 10% of above-peak device time sits on kernels exceeding their own cache-adjusted ceiling: the above-peak rates are consistent with cache service, the byte COUNTS stand, and the defect -- there is still a defect -- is that those bytes are priced at a DRAM rate when some of them never reached DRAM. REFUTED is the WEAK direction here, because the bound was deliberately built to be generous to exactly this explanation, and the artifact says so rather than reading a generous bound as a clean bill of health. ALSO REFUSED, independently of any share, IF THE ABOVE-PEAK POPULATION IS THIN: fewer than 10 movement kernels above the published peak. With no above-peak population the over-count share is 0% by construction, which reads as "the byte model is sound" -- a FINDING that would license every downstream byte figure in the campaign -- while meaning the selector found nothing to test, a DEFECT. Opposite in meaning, identical in arithmetic. That is the branch proved red before this cycle opened, by dropping every above-peak kernel from the population. I PREDICT REFUTED, in writing, before the run. The measured inflation is 1240.7 over 1008.0, a factor of 1.231, and a kernel can reach that under the cache reading whenever its working set is below about 384 MiB -- 72 MiB * 1.231 / 0.231. The large copies in this trace are checkpoint- and residual-scale rather than gigabyte-scale, so I expect most of them to sit under that size and be explained. I also expect that to be the LESS useful answer, because it leaves the byte counts standing while making the rate they are divided by wrong, which is harder to repair than a multiplier.

events.hypothesis: THE BOUND FALSIFIES A CONJUNCTION AND THE HYPOTHESIS NAMED ONLY ONE OF ITS TERMS. The ceiling assumes three things at once: the byte count is right, the kernel duration is right, and 1008.0 GB/s is this card's peak. Exceeding it falsifies their conjunction, not any single term. My hypothesis named the byte model, the criterion was frozen on it, and the verdict follows the criterion -- but the artifact does not get to convert that into a proof that bytes are the guilty term, and this update says so before anything downstream quotes it. THE MAGNITUDE POINTS AWAY FROM THE BYTES, AND THAT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING HERE. To bring 1240.7 under its 1084.2 ceiling the byte count would have to be inflated by a factor of 1.144. A byte model that miscounts traversals is wrong by a WHOLE TRAVERSAL -- 2x, 1.5x, 1.33x for two, three or four traversals counted as one more or one fewer. There is no traversal arithmetic that produces 14.4%. So the shape of the error does not look like the mechanism my own hypothesis named, and the term that would explain it cleanly is the REFERENCE: if this card sustains more than 1240.7 GB/s on a 1 GiB device-to-device copy, every one of these kernels is innocent and so is the byte model, and what is wrong is the specification figure the whole campaign divides by. WHY THAT IS NOT A LOOPHOLE I GET TO TAKE TODAY. 1008.0 GB/s is what a 384-bit bus at 21 Gbps yields, and a sustained rate 23% above it is not something a memory controller does. The remaining candidates are memory compression on the copy path, a duration that the profiler under-reports for these specific kernels, or dims that over-state the tensor -- and this cycle distinguishes none of them. What it establishes is that the three terms cannot all be right, which was not established before and which every lever in this campaign depends on. I PREDICTED REFUTED AND THE MEASUREMENT WENT THE OTHER WAY, at more than six times the threshold. My registered basis was that the large copies would be small enough for cache to explain -- I put the break-even at about 384 MiB and expected the trace's copies to sit under it. They are 1 GiB, nearly three times that size, and I had the trace on disk when I wrote the prediction. CACHE SERVICE: the bytes are real but part of the traffic never reached DRAM, in which case the byte COUNT is right and what is wrong is pricing those bytes at a DRAM rate, because some of them cost cache time instead of memory time. events.hypothesis: WHAT THE MODEL CHARGES, READ FROM ITS OWN SOURCE RATHER THAN ASSUMED. bytes_corrected for a movement op returns TRUE_TRAVERSALS[op] * max(sizes) -- for a copy, TWICE THE LARGEST recorded operand, not the sum of the operands. So 1,073,741,824 is 2 x a 512 MiB operand: one read and one write of the same-sized tensor. WHERE THAT FORMULA IS EXACT AND WHERE IT OVER-COUNTS. For a same-dtype copy source and destination are the same size and the kernel reads one and writes the other, so 2*max is exactly right. It over-counts precisely when the operands DIFFER in size, which is what a dtype-converting copy is: reading a bf16 source and writing an fp32 destination moves max + min, not 2*max. The maximum correction available from this mechanism is 2*max/(max+min), which for a bf16/fp32 pair is 1.333 and for equal operands is exactly 1.000. WHY THAT IS THE RIGHT DISCRIMINATOR FOR THIS QUESTION. Cycle 47 established that bringing 1240.7 under 1084.2 needs a factor of 1.144, and observed that no WHOLE-traversal miscount (2x, 1.5x, 1.33x) produces 14.4%. The operand-size mechanism is the one byte-side error that can produce a NON-integer ratio, because it depends on the dtype width ratio rather than on a traversal count. So it is the byte model's best remaining defence and its last chance to be the guilty term -- and testing it needs no bandwidth figure, no cache assumption and no occupancy counter, only the same trace read twice. THE BIAS, NAMED BEFORE THE RUN, AND IT POINTS AGAINST THE BYTES. The operand sum is a LOWER bound on real traffic: a strided or non-contiguous copy touches more than the sum of its operands, and a copy that also reads an index or mask touches more still. So the corrected rate computed here is an UPPER bound on the true achieved rate, which makes it HARDER for a kernel to fall under its ceiling. The substitution is therefore conservative against the traversal-count explanation, which means a SUPPORTED here would be the STRONG direction and this REFUTED, if it comes, is the weak one -- the opposite bias structure to cycles 42, 43 and 47, and the artifact says so rather than reading a conservative bound as a clean acquittal of the bytes.

events.hypothesis: WHAT THE REFUSALS BOUGHT, AND WHAT THEY DID NOT CLOSE. The instrument refused TWICE before it reported, at 0.6005 and then 0.8328 against a 0.85 coverage floor frozen before the run. Neither refusal was answered by lowering the floor. The first was cured by modelling backward contractions from their forward counterparts -- a backward records only its incoming-gradient shape -- and the second by deriving attention as the TWO contractions it actually performs (QK_T at (b*h, s, d, s) and AV at (b*h, s, s, d)) rather than charging it one averaged shape, since averaging two intensities either side of the ridge reports a boundary neither sits at. The second refusal also gained a residual listing: a refusal that does not name what it could not resolve ends the inquiry instead of directing it, and naming attention as the whole 11,970 us/step residual is what made the third run one patch away. THIS DOES NOT SAY THE GEMMS CURRENTLY RUN AT PEAK. Above the ridge means the arithmetic pipe is the binding constraint in a roofline sense, so a faster pipe CAN shorten the kernel. It is silent on whether these kernels are near their achievable rate today -- occupancy, tile quantisation, wave tails and epilogue cost are all unmeasured, and no occupancy counter exists anywhere in this campaign. So a 2x rate is an UPPER bound on what the precision route returns on this 91.3%, never a prediction of it. WHAT IT LEAVES OPEN FOR THE PRECISION ROUTE. Which of the two 2x carriers actually applies at each of these contractions is untested: FP8 is INCONCLUSIVE (row contractions measured faster than bf16 at forward 0.796 and dX 0.629 at m=4096, arm slower end to end on the wrapper and one dW event 2.72x its siblings) and FP16 ACCUMULATION has never been attempted at all and needs a cublasLt CUBLAS_COMPUTE_16F binding authored first. Nothing here adjudicates the #1413 loss bar for either. THE TAIL IS SMALL AND IS NOT ZERO. 0.8263 TF/step is traffic-bound, dominated by attention; mm at n=16 and n=1 and the two bmm rows are at 15.5, 1.0 and 0.7 FLOPs per byte and are rounding error in arithmetic while being real device time. aten::addmv_ at 10.7 us/step resolves no contraction at all.

events.observation: 91.3 percent of issued arithmetic is arithmetic-bound at the ridge, so a faster arithmetic pipe can shorten it, and bf16 does not fit the budget at any utilisation. Two carriers reach the published 2x rate on this card. FP8 is inconclusive. FP16 accumulation has never been attempted because torch does not expose the accumulator type -- torch.mm on half inputs always requests a 32F compute type, and the one precision harness in the tree binds _scaled_mm rather than cuBLASLt.

events.hypothesis: If cuBLASLt accepts CUBLAS_COMPUTE_16F for these operands and the resulting kernels run materially faster than the fp32-accumulate reference at the six contractions holding the most device time, then the 2x carrier with the smaller learning risk is reachable and the arm is worth a governed window. If it rejects the compute type, or accepts it and delivers no rate, the carrier is closed and FP8 is the only 2x route left.

events.refuted_if: REFUTED if cuBLASLt rejects CUBLAS_COMPUTE_16F at every one of the six measured shapes, OR if the median speedup over the fp32-accumulate reference across the accepting shapes is below 1.50x. The 1.50x line is arithmetic, not taste: at 60 percent end-to-end utilisation the measured 9.2100 TF/step costs 92.9 ms in bf16, and applying a speedup s to the 0.9105 eligible share gives 92.9 times (0.0895 plus 0.9105 over s), which is 64.7 ms at s equal to 1.5 and over the 51.2 ms budget. Below 1.5x this carrier cannot reach the terminal at a realistic utilisation.
events.supported_if: SUPPORTED if the compute type is accepted at the shapes holding the most device time and the median speedup is at or above 1.50x, with the relative L2 against the fp32-accumulate reference reported per shape and no tolerance asserted.

The statistic I froze does not answer the question the arithmetic I froze asks, so this run does not settle the route in either direction. Ruling SUPPORTED on the median would be selecting the favourable statistic after seeing the data, and ruling REFUTED on the time-weighted figure would be re-cutting a frozen criterion after seeing the data. The defect is mine and it is in the criterion, not in the measurement.

events.hypothesis: WHAT THIS RUN DID ESTABLISH, WHICH IS NOT NOTHING. (1) The binding exists: cuBLASLt is reachable by ctypes from the library torch itself loaded, and CUBLAS_COMPUTE_16F is ACCEPTED at all six measured contractions on this card. The carrier is not closed by the API. (2) The accumulator is GENUINELY HALF, proved numerically rather than assumed: the 16F path differs from the fp32-accumulate reference by 1.68e-03 relative L2 at every shape, against 0.0 to 3.3e-05 for the 32F path -- a separation of roughly two orders of magnitude, which is what a half accumulator looks like and what a silent fallback cannot produce. (3) Four of six shapes gain materially: 1.512x, 1.553x, 1.724x, 1.542x. THE FINDING THAT QUALIFIES THIS MORNING SHAPE RESULT, AND IT IS THE VALUABLE ONE. At m=2048 k=1024 n=1024 the 16F accumulator is ACTIVE -- its relative L2 is the same 1.68e-03 as everywhere else -- and it delivers 0.997x. No speedup at all. That contraction sits at 409.6 FLOPs per byte, two and a half times the 163.9 ridge, so the roofline classed it arithmetic-bound and predicted a faster pipe would shorten it. It did not. At m=1024 k=1024 n=256 (170.7 FLOPs per byte, just above the ridge) the gain is 1.114x. SO THE 91.3 PERCENT ARITHMETIC-BOUND SHARE IS AN UPPER BOUND ON WHAT THE PRECISION ROUTE CAN TOUCH, NOT A PREDICTION OF IT. Being above the ridge is necessary and is not sufficient; the registry row for that cycle already said a 2x rate is an upper bound and never a prediction, and this is the first measurement that shows the gap is real and large. THE INSTRUMENT DEFECT, CURED. The printed median took sorted()[n//2] on an even-length list, which is the UPPER middle value: it read 1.5419x where the median is 1.5270x. Favourable direction, again. Cured in place, with the arithmetic-versus-statistic requirement written into the docstring so the successor cannot inherit it. WHAT IS NOT CLOSED. The six shapes are the top of the census, not the census: they hold 33,138.4 of 71,674.3 us/step of eligible-site time, so 54 percent of it is unmeasured and the grouped-expert backward, the attention path and the 4,608-kernel m=1024 n=256 row are all outside the probe. Nothing here adjudicates the #1413 loss bar -- the relative L2 figures are reported with NO tolerance asserted, and a half accumulator over a full training step is a different question from one over a single contraction. And this is an ISOLATED-SHAPE probe: the FP8 arm had faster row contractions and was slower end to end.

THE CRITERION IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT AND THIS RUN FELL IN THE GAP. All six shapes accepted the compute type, so the first clause is not met. The median is 1.5270x, which CLEARS the 1.50x line. But the arithmetic the criterion quotes to justify that line applies s to a SHARE OF DEVICE TIME, and the time-weighted speedup those same six measurements give is 33,138.4 -> 23,951.3 us/step = 1.3836x, which FAILS it. The statistic I froze does not answer the question the arithmetic I froze asks, so this run does not settle the route in either direction. Ruling SUPPORTED on the median would be selecting the favourable statistic after seeing the data, and ruling REFUTED on the time-weighted figure would be re-cutting a frozen criterion after seeing the data. The defect is mine and it is in the criterion, not in the measurement.
hypotheses.not_closed: WHAT THIS RUN DID ESTABLISH, WHICH IS NOT NOTHING. (1) The binding exists: cuBLASLt is reachable by ctypes from the library torch itself loaded, and CUBLAS_COMPUTE_16F is ACCEPTED at all six measured contractions on this card. The carrier is not closed by the API. (2) The accumulator is GENUINELY HALF, proved numerically rather than assumed: the 16F path differs from the fp32-accumulate reference by 1.68e-03 relative L2 at every shape, against 0.0 to 3.3e-05 for the 32F path -- a separation of roughly two orders of magnitude, which is what a half accumulator looks like and what a silent fallback cannot produce. (3) Four of six shapes gain materially: 1.512x, 1.553x, 1.724x, 1.542x. THE FINDING THAT QUALIFIES THIS MORNING SHAPE RESULT, AND IT IS THE VALUABLE ONE. At m=2048 k=1024 n=1024 the 16F accumulator is ACTIVE -- its relative L2 is the same 1.68e-03 as everywhere else -- and it delivers 0.997x. No speedup at all. That contraction sits at 409.6 FLOPs per byte, two and a half times the 163.9 ridge, so the roofline classed it arithmetic-bound and predicted a faster pipe would shorten it. It did not. At m=1024 k=1024 n=256 (170.7 FLOPs per byte, just above the ridge) the gain is 1.114x. SO THE 91.3 PERCENT ARITHMETIC-BOUND SHARE IS AN UPPER BOUND ON WHAT THE PRECISION ROUTE CAN TOUCH, NOT A PREDICTION OF IT. Being above the ridge is necessary and is not sufficient; the registry row for that cycle already said a 2x rate is an upper bound and never a prediction, and this is the first measurement that shows the gap is real and large. THE INSTRUMENT DEFECT, CURED. The printed median took sorted()[n//2] on an even-length list, which is the UPPER middle value: it read 1.5419x where the median is 1.5270x. Favourable direction, again. Cured in place, with the arithmetic-versus-statistic requirement written into the docstring so the successor cannot inherit it. WHAT IS NOT CLOSED. The six shapes are the top of the census, not the census: they hold 33,138.4 of 71,674.3 us/step of eligible-site time, so 54 percent of it is unmeasured and the grouped-expert backward, the attention path and the 4,608-kernel m=1024 n=256 row are all outside the probe. Nothing here adjudicates the #1413 loss bar -- the relative L2 figures are reported with NO tolerance asserted, and a half accumulator over a full training step is a different question from one over a single contraction. And this is an ISOLATED-SHAPE probe: the FP8 arm had faster row contractions and was slower end to end.
hypotheses.closing: Ruled INCONCLUSIVE against a criterion whose statistic and whose arithmetic disagree across the decision line. The successor carries a TIME-WEIGHTED criterion over the whole eligible share, frozen before its own run, so the gap cannot recur. The binding, the numerical proof that the accumulator is genuinely half, and the above-the-ridge-yet-no-gain finding all stand and are registered.

THE FINDING WORTH MORE THAN THE VERDICT. FOUR INSTRUMENT DEFECTS, ALL FOUND BY ITS OWN GATES BEFORE ANY RATE WAS PUBLISHED, AND ONE OF THEM WAS AN OVER-CORRECTION OF ANOTHER. (b) That gate ran FIRST and pre-empted the deliberate red, so the red exited at a timing check instead of at the discriminator it exists to prove -- the identical defect the predecessor harness was repaired for one day earlier. events.observation: The time-weighted FP16 cycle closed REFUTED at 1.3591x and left behind a finding that governs more than the carrier it came from. Five of thirteen timed contractions -- 8,531.0 us/step, 19.8% of the timed set -- gained NOTHING from a demonstrably active half accumulator, and the roofline had classed every one of them arithmetic-bound, two of them at 2.5x and 3.1x the 163.9 FLOPs/byte ridge. m=2048 k=1024 n=1024 sits at 409.6 F/B and returns 1.008x. m=4096 k=1024 n=1024 sits at 455.1 F/B and returns 1.647x. Those two differ in m alone. So being above the ridge is NECESSARY and NOT SUFFICIENT, and the 91.3% arithmetic-bound share measured this morning is an UPPER BOUND on what any precision carrier can reach rather than a prediction of it. Every remaining precision candidate on this campaign -- FP8 included -- is sized against that share, so what actually decides the difference is worth more than the carrier that exposed it.

events.hypothesis: CANDIDATE MECHANISM: machine fill. A GEMM is tiled into T_m x T_n output tiles, each one CTA. This card has 128 SMs. A contraction producing fewer CTAs than that leaves SMs idle outright; one producing barely more runs a single wave plus a ragged tail. In either case the kernel is bounded by how much of the machine it occupies and by a prologue and epilogue it has no other wave to hide behind -- neither of which the arithmetic pipe's RATE touches. Doubling the rate of a pipe that is not saturated does nothing. CTAs = ceil(m/T_m) * ceil(n/T_n) is computable from shapes already recorded, so this needs no card, no counter and no profile. WHAT IS PREMISED: the tile. cuBLASLt selects it per shape and this instrument cannot observe that choice, so the claim is required to hold at THREE canonical tiles or it is a property of one guessed tile. WHAT IS MEASURED: the speedups and device times, from the rate receipt. THE PRIOR THIS GUARDS AGAINST: registry row the-empty-program-is-free-on-the-grouped-forward-and-costs-8-2-us-on-dw-20260915 records me reading a CTA count on 128 SMs as an occupancy win -- 384 programs against 1,536 -- and a 2x2 refuting it, with the grid term positive in both directions and the whole effect belonging to a different lever. A CTA count is a quantity that looks explanatory and has already misled this campaign once, which is why the criterion below carries a rival clause rather than only a separation clause.

events.refuted_if:
REFUTED if machine fill, computed as CTAs/128 from the recorded m and n, fails to separate the two groups at ANY of the three canonical tiles 128x128, 128x64 and 64x64 -- that is, if the MINIMUM wave count among contractions gaining 1.40x or more is not strictly above the MAXIMUM wave count among those gaining under 1.10x. Requiring it at all three tiles is what stops the result being a property of a tile I guessed.

ALSO REFUTED, and this is the clause that matters more, if any RIVAL quantity separates the same two groups just as cleanly: kernel duration, total FLOPs, output elements m*n, arithmetic intensity, contraction depth k, or census weight us/step, each asked in EITHER direction. A separation that a correlated quantity would also have produced explains nothing and cannot direct a measurement. The prior row above is exactly what an unguarded separation looks like when it is wrong.

SUPPORTED requires BOTH: fill separates at every tile AND no rival separates at all. Anything else -- fill separates but a rival does too, or fill separates at two tiles of three -- is at most INCONCLUSIVE, and the verdict will say which clause failed.

WHAT A SUPPORTED VERDICT WOULD AND WOULD NOT LICENSE. It would NOT prove the mechanism. Achieved occupancy, register pressure, shared-memory footprint, split-K decisions and the actually-selected tile are all unmeasured, and no counter for any of them exists anywhere in this campaign. It would license exactly one thing: that an occupancy measurement is the next instrument worth building, rather than one guess among several. That is a claim about where to point, and the criterion is frozen here, before the instrument runs, in both directions.

events.because:
THE MEASUREMENT IS CLEAN AND MY CRITERION IS NOT, SO THE VERDICT IS INCONCLUSIVE AND THE DEFECT IS MINE -- FOR THE SECOND CONSECUTIVE CYCLE.

What the instrument found. Machine fill separates the two groups at ALL THREE canonical tiles, with the same factor-of-two gap at each: 128x128 gaining 2.00-16.00 waves against flat 0.06-1.00; 128x64 gaining 4.00-32.00 against flat 0.06-2.00; 64x64 gaining 8.00-64.00 against flat 0.12-4.00. The boundary is MORE THAN ONE FULL WAVE of CTAs, and it does not depend on which tile is premised. The deliberate red -- the measured speedups reassigned in reverse rank, so the labels scramble while every geometric quantity stays exactly as measured -- refuses at all three tiles.

And the rival check, which is worth more than the separation: ARITHMETIC INTENSITY DOES NOT ORDER THESE GROUPS. Gaining spans 455.1-646.7 FLOPs/byte and the flat group includes 504.1 and 409.6, sitting INSIDE that range. Nor does kernel duration -- gaining spans 0.0586-0.435 ms and a flat shape sits at 0.409. Nor total FLOPs, nor contraction depth k, nor census weight. The roofline own variable fails to predict which contractions a faster arithmetic pipe shortens, and the count of output tiles succeeds.

WHY THIS IS NOT RULED SUPPORTED. The criterion I froze says two things that cannot both be applied: 'ALSO REFUTED ... if any RIVAL quantity separates the same two groups just as cleanly', and then 'Anything else ... is at most INCONCLUSIVE'. One rival did separate -- output elements m*n -- so the first clause says REFUTED and the second says INCONCLUSIVE, and the frozen text does not decide between them.

I also know which answer I would prefer, which is exactly why I am not taking it. m*n is not an independent rival: waves is ceil(m/T_m)*ceil(n/T_n)/SMs, a monotone function of m*n up to tile rounding, so it separates whenever fill does and its agreement is arithmetic rather than evidence. That is true, it was true before the instrument ran, and I only wrote it down AFTER the first red run showed the column fire. Excluding a rival from the frozen list after watching it fire is selecting the criterion to fit the data -- the identical move I refused in the FP16 cycle four hours ago and ruled INCONCLUSIVE for.

SO: INCONCLUSIVE, on the ground that the frozen criterion is internally inconsistent, not that the measurement failed. The measurement did not fail. Every number above stands on its own and none of it is withdrawn.

TWO INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT CRITERIA IN TWO CONSECUTIVE CYCLES IS A MECHANISM DEBT, NOT CARELESSNESS. Both have one shape: I wrote the criterion as PROSE, and prose admits two readings that only diverge once real numbers arrive. The cure is not more careful prose. It is that the instrument must COMPUTE and PRINT the verdict token from the frozen clauses, so the verdict is produced by code before I read any of it and cannot be adjudicated by interpretation afterwards. Applied to this instrument the same turn, so the successor inherits it.

events.hypothesis:
WHAT THIS CYCLE ESTABLISHED, INDEPENDENT OF THE VERDICT WORD.

1. ARITHMETIC INTENSITY DOES NOT PREDICT PRECISION GAIN AT THESE SITES, AND OUTPUT SIZE DOES. That is the campaign-level consequence and it is larger than the carrier that exposed it. Every precision candidate still standing -- FP8 above all -- has been sized against the morning 91.3% arithmetic-bound share, a figure computed entirely from FLOPs per byte. This cycle says that share is an upper bound on reach and not a prediction of it, and names the variable that does the predicting instead. Any future FP8 ceiling quoting an intensity-derived eligible share without a machine-fill filter is quoting a number this cycle has already shown over-predicts.

2. THE BOUNDARY IS ONE FULL WAVE, AND IT IS TILE-INVARIANT. Flat maxes at exactly one wave and gaining minimums at exactly two, at every premised tile. The invariance is what makes it worth anything: the tile is the one premise this instrument cannot observe, and the result does not depend on it.

WHAT IS NOT CLOSED.

3. THE MECHANISM IS NOT IDENTIFIED AND NO SHAPE ARITHMETIC CAN IDENTIFY IT. Machine fill and any other cost scaling with output size -- epilogue work per output element, store traffic, write-allocate behaviour -- are indistinguishable by construction here, because both are functions of m*n. This cycle narrows the question from why does the roofline over-predict to which output-size-scaling cost dominates, which is a smaller question and still an open one.

hypotheses.explanation: CANDIDATE MECHANISM: machine fill. A GEMM is tiled into T_m x T_n output tiles, each one CTA. This card has 128 SMs. A contraction producing fewer CTAs than that leaves SMs idle outright; one producing barely more runs a single wave plus a ragged tail. In either case the kernel is bounded by how much of the machine it occupies and by a prologue and epilogue it has no other wave to hide behind -- neither of which the arithmetic pipe's RATE touches. Doubling the rate of a pipe that is not saturated does nothing. CTAs = ceil(m/T_m) * ceil(n/T_n) is computable from shapes already recorded, so this needs no card, no counter and no profile. WHAT IS PREMISED: the tile. cuBLASLt selects it per shape and this instrument cannot observe that choice, so the claim is required to hold at THREE canonical tiles or it is a property of one guessed tile. hypotheses.observation:
The cycle closed minutes ago found that every lever this campaign has MEASURED -- all device idle, all elementwise time unexplained by bytes, and the FP16 contraction saving -- stacks to 1.7000x against the 3.4217x gate A needs. All three are the same KIND of lever: they run the same computational graph faster or with fewer gaps. The operator's distinction names the other kind, changing the graph so the same learning objective needs less work, and no cycle in this campaign has ever measured a candidate of that kind.

One is already half-visible in a landed receipt. optimizer-state-bytes-20260914T2041Z records, as an observation it explicitly did not investigate, that 844 of the 1,195 parameters in the optimizer param group have NEVER TAKEN A STEP at this head -- audio, image, all 14 router tensors, and experts 2 through 24, two of which the counter receipt lists as ACTIVE. It sized the stepped population at 474 M elements rather than 702 M, and then said in as many words that whether those tensors are meant to be receiving gradients is a separate question with a separate owner. With no second seat, that owner is me.

The registry query on this proposition's own nouns -- padding, masked positions, processed positions, redundant work, param groups never stepped -- returns nothing at all, and the source grep returns only membership constructions, no prior instrument.
hypotheses.explanation:
A parameter that never takes an optimizer step has no use for a gradient. If the backward computes one anyway, the arithmetic that produced it is device work that changes nothing: not work scheduled badly, not work in the wrong precision, but work that does not need to exist. Removing it is a change to the computational graph, which is the class of lever the stack result says the campaign must now find.

torch's autograd engine emits exactly one AccumulateGrad node per leaf tensor that actually receives a gradient in a backward pass. Counting them per optimizer step and comparing against the 351 tensors that carry AdamW state answers the question directly, from a trace already on disk, with no model of what the backward ought to do and no card.
hypotheses.criterion:
The criterion is computed IN CODE and printed as a verdict token before the tables are read. This states the same clauses in prose so a reader can check the implementation against them.

SUPPORTED if AccumulateGrad nodes per optimizer step exceed 1.20 times the stepped tensor count read from optimizer-state-bytes-20260914T2041Z. The backward then produces gradients for parameters nothing updates, and that work is removable by construction.

REFUTED if the ratio is at or below 1.05. Essentially every gradient the backward produces belongs to a parameter that is stepped and there is no work-removal lever at this site.

INCONCLUSIVE between the two lines, or if the optimizer receipt carries no stepped_set_composition, or if the trace carries no Optimizer.step# annotation to divide by.

THE DENOMINATOR IS DELIBERATELY THE LARGEST PLAUSIBLE ONE. Every distinct Optimizer.step# timestamp counts as a step, so if the profiler emits more than one annotation per real step the per-step figure and the ratio are UNDERSTATED -- the direction that argues AGAINST this hypothesis. My own record says both of my errors on an unwanted result ran favourable, so the bias is chosen against the result I expect rather than left to chance.

THIS COUNTS TENSORS, NOT ELEMENTS AND NOT MICROSECONDS, and that is registered before the run so a SUPPORTED cannot be read as more than it is. A one-element router tensor and a 33 M element expert weight each produce exactly one AccumulateGrad. A positive establishes that gradient work EXISTS for parameters nothing updates; it does not size that work, state a ceiling, license an arm, or produce a figure for what removing it would save. Sizing needs the per-tensor element counts joined to the backward contractions that produce them, which is a separate instrument that does not exist.

IT IS ALSO NOT A RULING THAT ANYTHING IS MISCONFIGURED. Whether those tensors are MEANT to be frozen at this head is a question about the training contract, and a frozen tensor that still receives a gradient is a defect while a tensor deliberately held out of the optimizer may be correct. This cycle measures which gradients exist and adjudicates neither.

WHAT NO OUTCOME LICENSES. No rate: the trace was captured UNDER PROFILING INSTRUMENTATION and this instrument quotes no duration at all. No occupancy, register-pressure, shared-memory or split-K counter exists in this build or anywhere in this campaign. One capture, one process, no matched-run variation. No model contract changes, no applied position, and no gate moves either way.

5,364 AccumulateGrad nodes over 12 distinct Optimizer.step# annotations is 447.0 per step against 351 tensors carrying AdamW state: ratio 1.2735, above the 1.20 line. Ninety-six tensors per optimizer step receive a gradient that no optimizer state consumes. The instrument computed the same token from the same clauses before its tables were printed.

THE MARGIN IS NARROW AND IS REPORTED AS NARROW. 1.2735 clears 1.20 by 0.07, not by a factor. The instrument takes every distinct Optimizer.step# timestamp as a step, which is the largest plausible denominator and therefore the smallest plausible ratio; a profiler emitting more than one annotation per real step makes the true ratio LARGER, not smaller. The bias was chosen before the run against the result I expected, because my own record says both of my errors on an unwanted result ran favourable.

BOTH BRANCHES WERE PROVED REACHABLE. Dropping every AccumulateGrad reports REFUTED; collapsing the denominator to one step reports SUPPORTED at 15.28.
hypotheses.not_closed:
WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES. The backward at this head produces gradients for about 96 tensors per optimizer step that carry no AdamW state and therefore take no step. That arithmetic is device work whose output is discarded. It is the first candidate this campaign has measured in the class the lever-stack result said it must now find: work that does not need to exist, rather than work that is scheduled badly or executed in the wrong precision.

WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH, AND THE FIRST ITEM IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS.

(1) IT SIZES NOTHING. The instrument counts TENSORS. A one-element router tensor and a 33 M element expert weight each produce exactly one AccumulateGrad, so 96 tensors could be microseconds or could be a large share of the backward, and nothing here distinguishes those. No ceiling is stated, no arm is licensed, and no figure for what removal would save exists. The successor is the instrument that joins these 96 to their element counts and to the backward contractions that produce them -- that is where a ceiling would come from and it does not exist yet.

(2) WHICH 96 IS UNKNOWN. The receipt names none of them. 844 tensors never step, so 748 of them correctly receive no gradient and 96 do; the split is measured and the membership is not. The optimizer receipt's own list of groups with no state -- audio, image, all 14 router tensors, experts 2 through 24 -- is where to look, and the routers are the obvious suspect because routing output is consumed by the forward whether or not the router learns.

(3) IT IS NOT A RULING THAT ANYTHING IS MISCONFIGURED, and that was registered before the run. A tensor deliberately held out of the optimizer while still receiving gradients may be exactly what the training contract intends; a tensor meant to be frozen that still computes gradients is a defect. This cycle measures which gradients exist and adjudicates neither, because the adjudication is a question about the learning contract.

(4) THE MARGIN DEPENDS ON THE STEP COUNT. 1.2735 clears the frozen 1.20 by 0.07. The denominator is 12 distinct Optimizer.step# annotations and the census elsewhere treats this trace as 6 windows; if 12 annotations are 6 real steps the ratio is 2.55, and if they are 24 the ratio is 0.64 and the verdict inverts. The chosen denominator is the largest plausible one and therefore the most conservative, but reconciling the annotation count against the real step count is owed and is not done here.

(5) NO RATE, NO SHARE, NO GATE. The trace was captured under profiling instrumentation and this instrument quotes no duration at all. No occupancy, register-pressure, shared-memory or split-K counter exists in this build or anywhere in this campaign. One capture, one process, no matched-run variation.

The rival explanation is that the two names mark different, non-overlapping work, in which case their sum is a legitimate count of gradient-related nodes and the predecessor's unit stands.

Both corrected ratios are BELOW 1.05, which is the predecessor own frozen REFUTED line -- so the corrected measurement does not merely fail to clear the SUPPORTED line, it lands in the refutation band.

BOTH BRANCHES WERE PROVED REACHABLE BEFORE THE RUN WAS TRUSTED. Shifting every inner event past the end of its outer event reports REFUTED at 0 of 2,538 nested. Removing the inner class entirely also reports REFUTED, on the sum clause rather than the nesting clause, so the two refusal grounds are exercised separately rather than the same one twice.

events.hypothesis:
WHAT THIS WITHDRAWS. The finding closed at 18:05Z today -- that the backward produces gradients for about 96 tensors per optimizer step that never take a step, recorded as this campaign's FIRST measured candidate in the work-REMOVAL class -- is withdrawn. Its counting predicate fused an autograd engine node with the op emitted inside it. Corrected, 235.5 gradient accumulations per step against 351 stepped tensors is a ratio of 0.6709: FEWER tensors receive a gradient than are stepped, which is the opposite of the published claim and is what a backward with no obvious waste looks like.

WHAT REPLACES IT, AND IT IS A REAL NUMBER RATHER THAN A RETRACTION ONLY. The inner op carries Input Dims, which the predecessor never read, so the gradient work is sized for the first time: 350,261,248 elements accumulated per optimizer step, every one of the 2,538 events carrying dims, against a stepped population of 474,030,080 elements in the optimizer receipt. The shape histogram is dominated by 3072x1024 (576), 1024x3072 (288), 2048x1024 (288) and 1024x1024 (288) -- the projection and expert matrices, not a tail of small tensors.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN, AND THE FIRST ITEM IS WHY THIS IS NOT A DEAD END.

(1) THE WORK-REMOVAL CLASS IS NOT REFUTED. What is refuted is one candidate's evidence. The lever-stack result still says roughly half the needed factor is on no route this campaign has measured, and graph-changing work-removal is still the class with no measured member. This cycle removes a false member; it does not close the class.

(2) NO ELEMENT IS ATTRIBUTED TO A NAMED TENSOR. The trace carries shapes, never names, so no share of the 350 M elements is assigned to a parameter that never steps. The join that would do it still does not exist.

(3) THE PLACEMENT MANIFEST SAYS 425 OF 1,195 PLACEMENTS REQUIRE GRAD against 351 carrying optimizer state, which is 74 tensors that require a gradient and have no state. That is a DIFFERENT checkpoint at a DIFFERENT head (the 2026-09-12 hour control) and requires_grad is a flag, not a measurement that a gradient was produced. The measured per-step accumulation count is below the stepped count, so those 74 are not demonstrated to cost anything. Whether any of them receives a gradient in a real step is open and this does not answer it.

(4) THE DENOMINATOR IS STILL OWED A RECONCILIATION. Twelve Optimizer.step# annotations are taken as twelve steps. Halving it doubles every per-step figure here exactly as it did for the predecessor -- at six steps the corrected ratio is 1.34 and the original claim would stand. The reconciliation was owed before this cycle and is owed after it, and it is now the single term that decides the question.

(5) NO RATE, NO DURATION, NO CEILING, NO GATE. Durations were used only as interval bounds to prove nesting. An element count is a size and does not convert to microseconds. One capture, one process, no matched-run variation.

THE MECHANISM DEBT, WHICH IS MINE. A substring test was used where an identity test was required, in an instrument whose whole output is a COUNT. The same class as taking a field by shape rather than by name. Any instrument whose headline is a count of events now matches event names exactly and prints the distinct matched names beside the count, so a fused class is visible in the output rather than invisible in the predicate.

events.observation: The step-annotation census over the captured trace finds 12 Optimizer.step#AdamW.step events that are NOT 12 steps' worth of one annotation each. They fall into exactly two categories of six: six 'user_annotation' events on tid 38448 (host, ~1.7 ms each) and six 'gpu_user_annotation' events on tid 7 (device, ~16 ms each). They strictly alternate in time, each device event beginning about 1.1 ms after its host neighbour starts, while consecutive pairs are separated by roughly 450,000 us. Every per-step figure this campaign has published from this trace divides by 12.

events.hypothesis: The profiler emits a user annotation twice for one annotated region: once on the host thread that opened the record_function scope, and once projected onto the device timeline as gpu_user_annotation covering the kernels that ran inside it. That is a rendering of one scope on two timelines, not two scopes. If so the trace contains SIX optimizer steps and the denominator 12 is a double count of exactly the same shape as the AccumulateGrad double count closed an hour ago: a predicate matching a name across two timelines rather than counting the thing the name denotes. Consequence, and it cuts against the cycle I just closed: at six steps the corrected engine-node figure is 2826/6 = 471.0 per step, ratio 1.3419 to 351 stepped tensors, which is ABOVE the withdrawn claim's frozen SUPPORTED line of 1.20 -- so the withdrawn finding would stand on the numerator correction plus this denominator correction together, the two errors having very nearly cancelled.

events.refuted_if: REFUTED if the split is not 6 and 6, or if the nearest-neighbour pairing is not a bijection (any host event whose nearest device event is already claimed, or any device event unpaired), or if the largest intra-pair offset is within 50x of the smallest inter-pair gap, or if the two categories carry different annotation names. Any one of these means the 12 events are not one scope rendered twice and the denominator 12 is not shown to be a double count.
events.supported_if: SUPPORTED if ALL of the following hold, each proved per event and not asserted from the names: (1) the 12 Optimizer.step# events partition into exactly two categories of exactly 6 each, one 'user_annotation' and one 'gpu_user_annotation'; (2) pairing each host event to its nearest-in-time device event is a strict BIJECTION -- 6 pairs, no host event claimed twice, no device event left over; (3) every pair's intra-pair start offset is smaller than the SMALLEST inter-pair gap by at least a factor of 50, so the two distributions are separable rather than merely ordered; (4) the paired device event lies inside or overlapping its host event's own name string, i.e. both carry the identical annotation name.

events.because:
The frozen criterion required four clauses, each proved per event. All four hold.

(1) The 12 Optimizer.step# events partition into exactly two categories of exactly six: six 'user_annotation' on tid 38448 and six 'gpu_user_annotation' on tid 7. (2) Nearest-in-time pairing is a strict bijection -- six pairs, no host event claimed twice, no device event left over. (3) The largest intra-pair offset is 1,175.9 us and the smallest inter-pair gap is 462,003.3 us, a separation of 392.9x against a required 50x, so the two distributions are separable rather than merely ordered. (4) Both categories carry the identical name, 'Optimizer.step#AdamW.step', the only annotation name in the trace.

SO THE TRACE CONTAINS SIX OPTIMIZER STEPS, NOT TWELVE. Twelve is one annotated scope rendered on two timelines, host and device, and counted once on each.

BOTH REDS HELD ON DIFFERENT CLAUSES, which is what makes the four clauses four checks rather than one. Relabelling every device annotation to the host category reports REFUTED on clauses 1, 2 and 4. Pushing each device annotation out toward the next pair leaves clauses 1, 2 and 4 TRUE and refutes on clause 3 alone, at a separation of 1.7x against the required 50x -- so the separability clause is load-bearing on its own and is not carried by the others.

events.hypothesis:
THIS CUTS AGAINST THE CYCLE I CLOSED AN HOUR AGO, AND IN THE DIRECTION THAT FLATTERS THE ORIGINAL CLAIM, SO IT GETS MORE SCRUTINY RATHER THAN LESS.

Two double counts, in opposite places, very nearly cancelling:
  numerator   -- 'AccumulateGrad' in name fused an autograd engine node with the op inside it: 2,826 + 2,538 = 5,364 where the engine-node count is 2,826.
  denominator -- twelve annotations fused a host scope with its device projection: six real steps where twelve were counted.
Published: 5,364 / 12 = 447.0, ratio 1.2735. Corrected on both: 2,826 / 6 = 471.0, ratio 1.3419 against 351 stepped tensors. The withdrawn row's own frozen SUPPORTED line was 1.20, so the corrected figure CLEARS IT -- by a wider margin than the figure that was published.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it does not re-rule that row. A verdict reinstated as a side effect of a different cycle's consequence block is a verdict nobody froze a criterion for. The re-ruling is the next cycle and it owes its own criterion before anything runs.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN.

(1) THE ANNOTATIONS ARE STEP MARKERS, NOT STEP SPANS. Zero of the 2,826 engine nodes fall inside any annotation interval; the host scope is about 1.7 ms and the device projection about 16 ms, while the inter-pair gap is about 462 ms. So dividing a whole-trace backward count by the marker count assumes the backward work is distributed evenly across the six steps. This cycle does not test that assumption, and a per-step figure built on it is a mean over the trace rather than a measurement of any one step.

(2) THE PAIRING IS EVIDENCE, NOT A READING OF THE PROFILER. Nearest-in-time plus name identity plus 392.9x separation is strong, and it is still an inference about how the profiler renders one scope. Reading the emitter would settle it outright and was not done.

(3) SIX STEPS IS A SMALL SAMPLE. Every per-step figure from this trace now rests on six intervals from one capture of one process under profiling instrumentation, with no matched-run variation.

(4) NO RATE, NO CEILING, NO GATE. The step count is a count. Nothing here converts to microseconds and no gate moves.

events.because:
All three frozen clauses hold at the installed torch header, and the verdict is SUPPORTED in the direction that costs me the margin.

(1) The inner per-node record is opened inside Node::operator(), which is the single entry point every autograd node invocation passes through. (2) The only condition guarding it is C10_UNLIKELY(step_callbacks.has_value()), where step_callbacks comes from at::getStepCallbacksUnlessEmpty(at::RecordScope::BACKWARD_FUNCTION). No term in that guard refers to gradient state, accumulation, assignment or stealing -- the instrument searched for grad, accumulate, defined(), steal and assign and found none. (3) The record is opened BEFORE the call to apply(), so it cannot depend on anything apply does, including which of accumulateGrad's cases runs.

If it does not, the unit may be the inner op, the ratio is 1.2051, and the conclusion survives while its margin does not. The shape route is already CLOSED -- engine nodes carry no Input Dims at all -- and the closing census named reading the autograd source as what would settle it.
hypotheses.explanation: The premise is a claim about WHEN the profiler emits the inner record, and that is readable. The installed wheel does not ship engine.cpp, so the ENGINE's emission of the outer record cannot be read here. It does ship torch/include/torch/csrc/autograd/function.h, which contains Node::operator() -- the single entry point every autograd node invocation passes through, and the place the per-node record is emitted. That is precisely the half the premise depends on: the benign explanation requires that a node can RUN and emit no record of its own. If the emission is guarded only by whether profiler step callbacks are active for the backward-function scope, and precedes the call to apply(), then nothing about assignment versus accumulation can suppress it -- apply() has not run yet when the record is opened -- and the benign explanation is refuted. Reading a header is text access: no import, no module load, no research code executed, no card, no lease.
hypotheses.criterion: REFUTED if the guard on the inner per-node emission contains any gradient-state term -- grad, accumulate, defined(), steal or assign -- so that a leaf whose gradient is assigned rather than accumulated could legitimately emit no inner record. In that case the 48-per-step gap has its benign explanation, the engine node stands as the unit, and 471 keeps its margin.
hypotheses.criterion_supported_if: SUPPORTED -- meaning the benign explanation is REFUTED -- if all three hold: (1) the inner per-node record is emitted inside Node::operator(), the single path every node invocation takes; (2) the only condition guarding it is the presence of profiler step callbacks for the backward-function scope, with no term referring to gradient state, accumulation, assignment or stealing; and (3) the emission precedes the call to apply(), so it cannot depend on what apply does. REFUSED rather than ruled if the header carries no such emission, which would mean the instrument is reading the wrong file.
hypotheses.instrument: scripts/issue1945/is_the_inner_accumulategrad_record_conditional.py
hypotheses.ruling:
All three frozen clauses hold at the installed torch header, and the verdict is SUPPORTED in the direction that costs me the margin.

(1) The inner per-node record is opened inside Node::operator(), which is the single entry point every autograd node invocation passes through. (2) The only condition guarding it is C10_UNLIKELY(step_callbacks.has_value()), where step_callbacks comes from at::getStepCallbacksUnlessEmpty(at::RecordScope::BACKWARD_FUNCTION). No term in that guard refers to gradient state, accumulation, assignment or stealing -- the instrument searched for grad, accumulate, defined(), steal and assign and found none. (3) The record is opened BEFORE the call to apply(), so it cannot depend on anything apply does, including which of accumulateGrad's cases runs.

THEREFORE THE BENIGN EXPLANATION IS REFUTED. A leaf whose .grad is assigned rather than accumulated still runs the same operator() and still emits the same record. Assignment versus accumulation cannot produce the 48-per-step gap.

BOTH REDS HELD ON DIFFERENT GROUNDS: a mutated header whose guard tests inputs[0].grad().defined() reports REFUTED on clause 2 while clauses 1 and 3 still pass, so clause 2 is carrying its own weight; a mutated header with the emission deleted REFUSES rather than ruling either way, so the instrument cannot report an answer from a file that is not the emission site.
hypotheses.not_closed:
WHAT THIS DOES TO THE 471 FIGURE. It removes its explanation and leaves its arithmetic standing. The registry recorded the 48-per-step gap as CONSISTENT WITH leaves whose gradient is assigned rather than accumulated, and explicitly refused to call that demonstrated. It is now refuted: the emission is unconditional on the gradient path. So 48 nodes per step have an outer evaluate_function record and no record of their own, and nothing readable here says why.

THE HONEST POSITION ON THE UNIT. At 471 engine nodes the ratio to 351 stepped tensors is 1.3419; at 423 inner ops it is 1.2051. Both clear the 1.20 line the predecessor row froze for itself, so the CONCLUSION -- more leaves receive gradients than have optimizer state -- survives either unit. The MARGIN does not: 0.14 versus 0.005. Every statement of that finding now carries both numbers, and the excess is 120 leaves per step at one unit and 72 at the other.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN, NARROWED TO ONE THING. The wheel does not ship engine.cpp, so what makes the ENGINE emit an outer evaluate_function record for a node whose own record never appears is not readable on this host. The candidate mechanism worth testing next is the engine's exec_info needed_ path -- a node reached by the graph walk but not executed because nothing downstream needs it -- which would make the 48 nodes evaluated-but-skipped rather than executed, and would make the INNER op the right unit. That is a source question, not a trace question, and settling it needs either a torch source distribution or a fresh capture that distinguishes the two.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE. It says nothing about which leaves are in the excess, nothing about cost -- still a count of graph work and not microseconds -- and nothing about any rate or ceiling. NO GATE MOVES.
hypotheses.closing: Ruled SUPPORTED on all three frozen clauses, both reds held. The inner per-node profiler record is emitted inside Node::operator(), guarded only by the presence of backward-scope profiler callbacks, before apply() is called. Assignment versus accumulation therefore cannot suppress it, and the benign explanation for the 48-per-step gap between 2,826 outer and 2,538 inner events is refuted. The 471 unit loses its justification while its arithmetic stands: the ratio is 1.3419 at the engine node and 1.2051 at the inner op, and both clear the frozen 1.20 line, so the conclusion survives either unit and the margin does not. Not closed: the engine's own emission rule is not readable on this host, and the exec_info needed_ skip path is the candidate mechanism nobody has tested.
